item.title: Duce Robinson injury update is brutal news for Florida State
item.description: Florida State will play the rest of the 2026 season not only with an interim head coach, but also without one of its best players. According to On3’s Pete Nakos , FSU wide receiver Duce Robinson will miss the rest of the 2026 season with a torn ACL. MORE : Florida State fires Mike Norvell after Saturday’s Clemson loss He got injured during FSU’s 36-24 loss against Clemson on Saturday. He finished the game with two receptions for 31 yards. Duce Robinson’s 2026 season Sep 6, 2025; Tallahassee, Florida, USA; Florida State Seminoles wide receiver Duce Robinson (0) catches a pass over East Texas A&M Lions cornerback Kaleb Miles (1) during the first half at Doak S. Campbell Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Melina Myers-Imagn Images This is a big loss for the Seminoles since Robinson is their best wideout. He leads the team in receptions, receiving yards, and touchdowns with 24 catches for 438 yards and four touchdowns. Nobody can separate like him or make the catches he makes. Seminoles quarterback Ashton Daniels will need to rely on his other wideouts, such as Jayvan Boggs, for the rest of the year. Boggs leads the team in receiving yards with 415 and has one touchdown this year. The Seminoles are 3-5 through eight games and will try to get their fourth win when they face the Boston College Eagles this Saturday. Kickoff will be at noon ET. — Enjoy free coverage of the top news & trending stories with The Big Lead Newsletter —

item.title: Oscar Goodman makes first start in Michigan's opener: 'Means a lot'
item.description: ANN ARBOR — Michigan coach Mike Boynton Jr. had several options and different ways he could’ve gone. With big man Moustapha Thiam missing the season opener against Oakland with an illness, Boynton could’ve inserted freshman Quinn Costello or veteran Jalen Reed at the power forward spot. He could’ve gone smaller and went with Ricky Liburd in the starting lineup. Instead, Boynton opted to give Oscar Goodman the nod and the first start of his college career. “I just thought Oscar has earned an opportunity,” Boynton said after Michigan’s 84-68 win at Crisler Center on Monday, Nov. 2. It’s one Goodman has been waiting for and working toward after joining the program midseason two years ago. The New Zealand native spent his first year on the scout team. Last season, he saw limited playing time primarily at the end of games while playing behind a loaded frontcourt that featured three lottery picks. On Monday, Goodman played meaningful minutes for the first time and had some good moments. In the first half, he grabbed a defensive rebound and threw a long outlet pass to J.P. Estrella for a fast-break layup. In the second half, he had a Euro-step finish in transition during a 9-0 run that put the game out of reach. He finished with six points, five rebounds, two assists, two steals and a blocked shot. He logged a career-high 22 minutes — double his previous high of 11 minutes last season. And while he shot 0-for-5 from 3-point range on a night the Wolverines were cold from deep, he didn’t stop letting it fly whenever he got a clean look. “I thought he played well enough,” Boynton said. “He was one of those guys that (had a) bunch of open shots, took good shots. What I'm glad is it didn't discourage him from rebounding and flying around on the defensive end because he still made a real positive impact on the game.” That showed in the plus-minus rating, where Goodman was a plus-23 against the Golden Grizzlies. That was the second-best mark on the team behind Estrella’s plus-25 rating. “I think I did pretty well,” said Goodman, who dealt with a tweaked back in the preseason. “I came out with some rebounds when we needed them and just kept shooting the ball. I need to keep shooting it, just stay confident in myself and they're going to drop eventually.” A little Euro step from the New Zealander‼️ 📺: @BigTenNetwork pic.twitter.com/S6Oda6aOhF — Michigan Men's Basketball (@umichbball) November 3, 2026 According to Goodman, Boynton informed him during Sunday’s practice that Thiam was going to be out and he was going to start. For someone who had to wait his turn and sacrificed playing time that he could’ve received elsewhere, getting that opportunity “means a lot.” “It was awesome. I called my parents. My brother is in town, so that was cool for him to see that,” Goodman said. “I was really excited, really happy for the moment, knowing the past year was put to good use. “I've never really not played before in my career. item.content:encoded: ANN ARBOR — Michigan coach Mike Boynton Jr. had several options and different ways he could’ve gone. Instead, Boynton opted to give Oscar Goodman the nod and the first start of his college career. “I just thought Oscar has earned an opportunity,” Boynton said after Michigan’s 84-68 win at Crisler Center on Monday, Nov. 2. It’s one Goodman has been waiting for and working toward after joining the program midseason two years ago. The New Zealand native spent his first year on the scout team. On Monday, Goodman played meaningful minutes for the first time and had some good moments. In the first half, he grabbed a defensive rebound and threw a long outlet pass to J.P. Estrella for a fast-break layup. In the second half, he had a Euro-step finish in transition during a 9-0 run that put the game out of reach. He finished with six points, five rebounds, two assists, two steals and a blocked shot. He logged a career-high 22 minutes — double his previous high of 11 minutes last season. And while he shot 0-for-5 from 3-point range on a night the Wolverines were cold from deep, he didn’t stop letting it fly whenever he got a clean look. “I thought he played well enough,” Boynton said. “He was one of those guys that (had a) bunch of open shots, took good shots. What I'm glad is it didn't discourage him from rebounding and flying around on the defensive end because he still made a real positive impact on the game.” That showed in the plus-minus rating, where Goodman was a plus-23 against the Golden Grizzlies. That was the second-best mark on the team behind Estrella’s plus-25 rating. “I think I did pretty well,” said Goodman, who dealt with a tweaked back in the preseason. “I came out with some rebounds when we needed them and just kept shooting the ball. I need to keep shooting it, just stay confident in myself and they're going to drop eventually.” A little Euro step from the New Zealander‼️ 📺: @BigTenNetwork pic.twitter.com/S6Oda6aOhF — Michigan Men's Basketball (@umichbball) November 3, 2026 According to Goodman, Boynton informed him during Sunday’s practice that Thiam was going to be out and he was going to start. For someone who had to wait his turn and sacrificed playing time that he could’ve received elsewhere, getting that opportunity “means a lot.” “It was awesome. I called my parents. My brother is in town, so that was cool for him to see that,” Goodman said. “I was really excited, really happy for the moment, knowing the past year was put to good use. “I've never really not played before in my career. I think that little bump in the journey helped me out a bit with resilience. I think ultimately it's made me a better player.” So did practicing against Morez Johnson Jr., Yaxel Lendeborg and Aday Mara last season. Seeing Mara’s footwork and how he uses angles, Johnson’s motor and relentlessness on the glass, and Lendeborg’s ability to be a big guard who can do a bit of everything are all things Goodman has tried to take and add to his game. The same could be said about learning from another talented big in Thiam, who practiced Saturday but didn’t Sunday. Boynton is hopeful Thiam’s regular-season debut will only be delayed by a few days, and he’ll return for Friday’s national title rematch against UConn in Boston. “I want to try as best I can not to play doctor when I’m in here,” Boynton said, “but I do believe just based off what we know, Moustapha’s just got something that’s like a 48-hour bug. He had a bit of a temperature, so we thought it’d be best to let him rest.” Regardless of Thiam’s availability, Goodman said moving forward he needs to keep trusting his shot and crash the glass harder. And as the longest-tenured scholarship player on the roster, he feels a responsibility to be a leader and bring the team together, no matter if he’s starting or coming off the bench. Depth was a strength of Michigan’s last season and Goodman will have a say whether that remains the case. Boynton believes Goodman can be a connector on offense and provides defensive versatility that allows the Wolverines to be a good switching team. Yet, Boynton added Goodman is among those who are “showing signs occasionally.” The next step is finding consistency — from possession to possession, from half to half, from game to game. “He did a good job,” Estrella said of Goodman. “He was gritty, tough. I mean, that's what we need out of him every single night.” jhawkins@detroitnews.com @jamesbhawkins This article originally appeared on The Detroit News: Oscar Goodman makes first start in Michigan's opener: 'Means a lot'

item.title: LeBron’s Wine Sip Proves The 76ers Are Finally Having Fun
item.description: Bill Streicher-Imagn Images During Monday night’s contest versus the Chicago Bulls, LeBron James sampled some red wine belonging to a fan. The Philadelphia 76ers won that matchup 126 to 107. James finished with 15 points, 7 rebounds, and 9 assists while the team moved to a 7-1 record on the season. The star player is no longer just grinding through the long season; he is enjoying the ride again. The moment happened in the third quarter when James chased a loose ball and crashed into fan Troy Clemons. Clemons was holding a cup of red wine, which is James’ favorite drink. James spilled some of the wine on himself and decided to taste it right there on the floor. He later told reporters, “I wanted to see if it was worth it on my arm, how good it was. It was all right,” per ESPN . This wasn’t a planned stunt or a media event. It was a spontaneous reaction to a messy play. Sports often feel like a serious job for players, but this incident shows James treating the game like a party. He danced after an and-one layup that made guard Tyrese Maxey laugh. He also danced with Maxey later when the point guard scored his own and-one basket. These are the small moments that keep a player fresh. James explained the need for this joy clearly. He said, “Listen, it’s a long marathon. If you don’t find ways to have fun throughout it, even though you’re working, even though you’re locked in, then it could wear on you,” according to ESPN. Clemons, the fan who lost his wine, did not mind the exchange at all. He told ESPN, “I’m just glad for him to be here.” He even added, “I’m not worried about the wine getting on me.” The fan threw the cup away and got a fresh drink. He now has a story that will last a lifetime. The 76ers are 7-1, and the atmosphere in the arena feels lighter. This is what a winning team looks like when the players are actually happy. A Pattern of Fun in Philadelphia James has a history of playful moments involving alcohol during games. After missing a shot in 2017, he seized a beer bottle from a vendor, feigned drinking from it, then returned the bottle. That was a different time, but the spirit remains the same. On Monday, the interaction was more direct and personal. ESPN’s Kris Rhim posted a video of the event on X, captioning it, “Here’s vid of LeBron taking a sip of a drink from a fan just now during tonight’s game.” The video went viral because it felt real and unscripted. The 76ers face the Detroit Pistons on Wednesday. The Pistons are the only team to beat Philadelphia this season. The team needs to keep this fun energy if they want to stay on top. James noted that the fans are great to them, so they try to be great to the fans by playing hard and being showmen. The wine sip was just one part of a great game for the Sixers. The numbers show they are winning, but the smile on James’ face shows they are enjoying it. The final score was 126-107, and the team took a wine sip. item.title: Eduardo Camavinga talks Vinicius, Mourinho, Bernardo Silva, Real Madrid future and personal transformation ahead of AEK Athens clash
item.description: Eduardo Camavinga talks Vinicius, Mourinho, Bernardo Silva, Real Madrid future and personal transformation ahead of AEK Athens clash Real Madrid are looking to continue their winning run when they face AEK Athens in the UEFA Champions League on Wednesday. Los Blancos come into this game with six consecutive wins, and Jose Mourinho will want his team to keep up the momentum in Greece. Ahead of the encounter, Eduardo Camavinga spoke openly about his difficult summer, his relationship with Jose Mourinho and the changes he made to his preparations. On his difficult summer and personal transformation The French midfielder began his press conference by expressing his condolences following the tragic death of Tenerife footballer Jesus de Miguel. “First, before we begin, I would like to express my condolences to the family of Jesus de Miguel,” he said. Reflecting on the uncertainty surrounding his future, Camavinga admitted: “To be honest, it was a tough, difficult time for me.” Eduardo Camavinga is likely to start alongside Bernardo Silva for Real Madrid tomorrow. (Photo by Angel Martinez/Getty Images) “I’ve worked very hard this summer, and I’m a new man. I have more discipline than before. I’m working to repay the trust the club has placed in me,” he explained. Explaining his transformation, he added: “I went back to school, it was a very different experience.” “I worked on things I don’t usually do, discipline, for instance, arriving two or three hours early to work in the gym. My mindset has also changed. I’m a bit more mature.” Camavinga on Mourinho, Vinicius and Bernardo Silva Camavinga also praised Mourinho’s influence on his development and spoke about his relationship with the manager. “He’s a very likeable person, he’s a great coach with a rich history. You learn a lot from him every day, about the mindset you need to have on the pitch,” the Frenchman said. The 23-year-old was then quizzed on whether he could have imagined Vinicius Jr. leaving the club back in the summer. “Actually, no, I wouldn’t, because Vini has been a Madridista since he was a child. He loves the club. I would never imagine that he would want to leave,” he said. On Bernardo Silva, he said: “He’s a great player. He helps us a lot in possession and build-up.” Camavinga speaks about dressing-room unity Camavinga dismissed suggestions that Real Madrid’s earlier struggles were due to a lack of unity in the dressing room. “We have always had a good relationship, we have always been a united team. But when the results aren’t good, you assume there’s something wrong in the dressing room,” he said. Camavinga’s fortunes are slowly improving at Real Madrid. (Photo by Denis Doyle/Getty Images) Finally, the French midfield star spoke about Real Madrid’s ambitions. “Our job is to win every match. We’ve started the season well, and we need to keep it up,” he concluded. Camavinga’s appearance before the media ahead of the game suggests he is likely to start against AEK Athens tomorrow. Au

His younger counterpart could take that role tomorrow, playing alongside Bernardo Silva as Madrid look to secure another three points. Camavinga was very candid about his recent struggles and how he has changed as a footballer, and it remains to be seen how he fares against AEK Athens tomorrow. Quotes source: Mundo Deportivo

item.title: Four Herald News field hockey teams advance to the MIAA playoffs
item.description: All four Herald News field hockey team each punched their ticket to the MIAA playoffs this fall. The two-time reining Division 2 state champion No. 4 Somerset Berkley will host a Round of 32 game. Durfee, No. 31, travels to Franklin for a Round of 32 matchup. In Division 4 action, both No. 18 Westport and No. 25 Joseph Case travel on the road for their Round of 32 games. Here's a look at the opening matchups for playoffs: Watch MA high school sports on NFHS Joseph Case Cardinals Record: 2-11-5 Seed: No. 25 in Division 4 Opening matchup: Travels to No. 8 Manchester Essex (10-4-3) in the Round of 32 at Manchester Essex High School. Durfee Hilltoppers Record: 10-7-1 Seed: No. 31 in Division 1 Opening matchup: Travels to No. 2 Franklin (15-1-2) in the Round of 32 at Franklin High School. Somerset Berkley Raiders Record: 15-2-1 Seed: No. 4 in Division 2 Opening matchup: Hosts No. 29 Wayland (5-12-1) in the Round of 32 at Somerset Berkley Regional High School. Westport Wildcats Record: 12-2-3 Seed: No. 17 in Division 4 Opening matchup: Travels to No. 16 Hamilton-Wenham (9-8-1) in the Round of 32 at Hamilton-Wenham Regional High School. item.title: 76ers' Tyrese Maxey makes franchise history only Allen Iverson, Wilt Chamberlain have made
item.description: 76ers' Tyrese Maxey makes franchise history only Allen Iverson, Wilt Chamberlain have made originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . While LeBron James, Jaylen Brown and Joel Embiid get most of the attention for the Philadelphia 76ers , it is Tyrese Maxey who should really be putting fear into opposing teams. The guard out of Kentucky is one of the shiftiest players in the entire NBA. Maxey continues to get better with every game. Over the weekend, in a game where James and Embiid were both sidelined, he went nuclear. “Tyrese Maxey tonight as the 76ers improve to 6-1 this season: 38 points (15 in 4Q), 4 rebounds, 4 assists, 2 steals. This is the third time this season that he has scored 15+ points in the fourth quarter,” ClutchPoints wrote. On Monday, it was more of the same for Maxey, particularly in the fourth quarter, when he took over the game. It wasn't a particularly high-scoring night for the guard — at least until the fourth quarter. “Tyrese Maxey scored 15 of his 26 points in the fourth quarter and dished out 11 assists to highlight the Philadelphia 76ers' 126-107 victory over the visiting Chicago Bulls on Monday,” The News Tribune wrote. In the game against the Chicago Bulls, Maxey made franchise history, joining an exclusive group that includes some of the greatest players to ever wear a 76ers uniform. Maxey became just the third player in franchise history to accomplish the feat, joining Allen Iverson and Wilt Chamberlain. “Tyrese Maxey is the third player in 76ers history with 20+ games of 25 points and 10 assists, joining Allen Iverson (65) and Wilt Chamberlain (25),” ESPN’s Kris Rhim posted. This shows just how special Maxey is, especially with so many weapons around him to whom he can distribute the ball. While he has a knack for scoring, it is also clear that he can set his teammates up and get them involved. The guard out of Kentucky has been a special find for Philadelphia since he was drafted, and he continues to prove that. Now, playing alongside some of the best in the world, his game continues to evolve, with his latest accomplishment putting him in the history books alongside 76ers legends. More MLB news: Lakers' Luka Doncic reveals where his game has improved the most during the new era in LA Spurs' Victor Wembanyama takes indirect shot at 76ers' LeBron James, Heat's Giannis Antetokounmpo Mavericks’ Kyrie Irving gets major trade update from NBA insider as future in Dallas becomes clear Warriors predicted to part ways with ex-Celtics' $20M NBA champion amid ongoing health battle

The guard out of Kentucky has been a special find for Philadelphia since he was drafted, and he continues to prove that. Now, playing alongside some of the best in the world, his game continues to evolve, with his latest accomplishment putting him in the history books alongside 76ers legends. item.title: Steelers DC Patrick Graham ranked one of the the NFL’s best new coordinators
item.description: Mandatory Credit: Barry Reeger-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Sunday, as Pittsburgh moved to 6-2 and gained sole possession of first place in the AFC North. The Steelers’ defense has come alive over the last month, thanks to their new defensive coordinator, Patrick Graham. CBS Sports ranked the NFL’s best new coordinators at midseason , and Graham earned the number two spot overall on the list. “The Pittsburgh Steelers’ defense has come back to life under new defensive coordinator Patrick Graham,” Garrett Podell writes. “They’re the league’s No. 3 scoring defense (18.0 points per game allowed), No. 6 total defense (305.6 total yards per game allowed), No. 3 run defense (83.9 rushing yards per game allowed), No. 8 third down defense (34.3% third down conversion rate allowed), No. 2 red zone defense (37.5% third down conversion rate allowed), and tied for No. 3 in takeaways (13).” “Having All-Pro edge rusher T.J. Watt turning back the clock also helps. After he had just 7.0 sacks in 14 games last season, Watt has 7.5 in eight games this season, which is tied for the league lead with Houston Texans All-Pro edge rusher Will Anderson Jr. No team has more sacks in the NFL than Graham’s unit’s 26, one more than the Brian Flores blitzkrieg Minnesota Vikings attack. ” “The Browns were flying high entering Week 8 with a 5-2 record, but they left Pittsburgh 5-3 after a 27-6 defeat in which the Steelers held them to both season-lows in points (6) and rushing yards (34). Graham is crushing it.” Graham was behind only Packers defensive coordinator Jonathan Gannon on the list. Graham joined the Steelers staff after spending the previous four seasons as the defensive coordinator of the Las Vegas Raiders. Graham’s zone-heavy defense has done wonders for the unit. Take this past weekend, for example, as the team recorded eight sacks against Cleveland. The Steelers can finally say they once again have an elite defense to help them in their playoff push as they enter the second half of their 2026 campaign. With Graham in charge and the abundance of talent on the unit, it seems like the Steelers are destined to have their first top-10 scoring defense since the 2023 season. Graham deserves all of the praise he is getting from the media. Let us know what you think in the comments . item.title: ‘So fake’… NBA fans react to LeBron James saying he enjoyed being Russell Westbrook’s teammate
item.description: Photo by Jason Miller/Getty Images LeBron James has paid tribute to former teammate Russell Westbrook – but fans are not buying it. Russell Westbrook announced his retirement from the NBA in the offseason, ending a long career that peaked by winning the MVP in the 2016-17 season. He became the first player to ever average a triple-double for an entire season. Westbrook’s jersey will be retired by the Oklahoma City Thunder, and his former LA Lakers teammate LeBron James has paid tribute to him, speaking to the Mind The Game podcast . James said: “I think one of the things about Russ that doesn’t get talked about is like the guy never wanted to take a night off. Wanted to play in every single game. Being a teammate of his for that year or two, I think it was a year and a half, maybe two years in LA. He never wanted to take a game off. “Never wanted to take a practice off. Great dude. You can never, it’s not going to be one person that played with him in the locker room and he like, man, he wasn’t a good teammate like, everyone raves about him, including myself. “Kudos to him and that jacket, that Hall of Fame jacket is next.” The Lakers traded for Westbrook in 2021, striking a deal with the Wizards in exchange for Kyle Kuzma, Kentavious Caldwell-Pope, Montrezl Harrell, and a 2021 first-round pick. The move was a spectacular failure, with ball-dominant Westbrook and James failing to gel on the court. The Lakers won only 33 games in 2021-22, having lost key depth including Alex Caruso, who was allowed to walk for financial reasons. Frank Vogel was fired and replaced by Darvin Ham, who relegated Westbrook into a bench role. The Lakers eventually traded Westbrook to the Jazz in February 2023. LeBron James slammed for Westbrook comments LeBron James’ tribute to Russell Westbrook has raised eyebrows, after their dysfunctional time on the Lakers together. One fan wrote on social media: “Bron knows deep down he hated playing with him.” A second fan hit out: “LeBron is so fake. He was begging the Lakers to get rid of Russell Westbrook.” Another added: “He just playing it up for the camera, we all know Russ was a locker room vampire.” A third fan noted: “There’s always such an obvious lack of enthusiasm when he talks about Russ.” And another comment added: “Says the dude who used him as a scapegoat.” James eventually moved on from the LA Lakers earlier this year, signing with the Philadelphia 76ers. The 41-year-old appears to be enjoying his basketball a lot more right now than during the Lakers-Westbrook era – which might just have been the least enjoyable from James’ career, at least looking from the outside. item.title: 10 takeaways from Oregon State’s loss at Fresno State
item.description: FRESNO, Calif. — Oregon State lost to Fresno State 38-22 Saturday night at Valley Children’s Stadium. Here are 10 takeaways as the Beavers prepare to host Texas State. 1. Reality check Two things can be true. Oregon State can still be ahead of schedule and on its way to a legitimately surprising season amid a massive rebuild, complete with a potent offense. Much of its success thus far came by pounding less talented teams and several of the worst defenses in the country. And where OSU was vulnerable was there to be exploited by teams like Fresno State, which has talent and good coaching. The Beavers are not a College Football Playoff team. That dose of reality doesn’t diminish what’s being accomplished this season. They’re simply not one of the two most talented teams in the Pac-12 right now. 2. Oregon State was outcoached JaMarcus Shephard and his staff were outcoached for definitely the first time in conference play and arguably for the first time this season. Matt Entz laid out in detail what Fresno State picked up from studying Braden Atkinson from his time at Mercer and Oregon State’s tendencies. Bye weeks also include self-scouting. Fresno State was more prepared for what OSU showed and particularly offensively the Beavers did not have an effective counter. 3. Self-inflicted errors can’t happen in games like this Winning on the road against a team with at least comparable (if not better) talent and coaching is a difficult task to begin with. It becomes a whole lot harder with six presnap penalties and allowing five sacks with two leading to fumbles. OSU absolutely could have led by multiple scores early if not for a false start negating Jake Reichle’s would-be touchdown, if Aeryn Hampton’s foot was in bounds and if multiple other penalties didn’t occur. That doesn’t even get into defensive miscues from missed tackles or over-pursuits. 4. The offensive line may have had its worst game Houston was more physically dominating than Fresno State, but that’s to be expected. Oregon State’s offensive line had a brutal showing nearly across the board, with sacks allowed by multiple players in one-on-one matchups. OSU’s rushing stats are skewed by the sacks and not nearly as poor as the final box score, but the bottom line is Fresno State won the line of scrimmage and it’s not a particularly stout group. 5. Josiah Freeman was the best receiver on the field Fresno State’s 6-foot-4 receiver had a big night with two touchdowns. Freeman had a massive advantage against Isaiah Houi and performed accordingly. But an outside target like him is hard to beat and he showed why. 6. item.content:encoded: FRESNO, Calif. — Oregon State lost to Fresno State 38-22 Saturday night at Valley Children’s Stadium. Here are 10 takeaways as the Beavers prepare to host Texas State. 1. Reality check Two things can be true. Oregon State can still be ahead of schedule and on its way to a legitimately surprising season amid a massive rebuild, complete with a potent offense. Much of its success thus far came by pounding less talented teams and several of the worst defenses in the country. And where OSU was vulnerable was there to be exploited by teams like Fresno State, which has talent and good coaching. The Beavers are not a College Football Playoff team. That dose of reality doesn’t diminish what’s being accomplished this season. They’re simply not one of the two most talented teams in the Pac-12 right now. 2. Oregon State was outcoached JaMarcus Shephard and his staff were outcoached for definitely the first time in conference play and arguably for the first time this season. Matt Entz laid out in detail what Fresno State picked up from studying Braden Atkinson from his time at Mercer and Oregon State’s tendencies. Bye weeks also include self-scouting. Fresno State was more prepared for what OSU showed and particularly offensively the Beavers did not have an effective counter. 3. Self-inflicted errors can’t happen in games like this Winning on the road against a team with at least comparable (if not better) talent and coaching is a difficult task to begin with. It becomes a whole lot harder with six presnap penalties and allowing five sacks with two leading to fumbles. OSU absolutely could have led by multiple scores early if not for a false start negating Jake Reichle’s would-be touchdown, if Aeryn Hampton’s foot was in bounds and if multiple other penalties didn’t occur. That doesn’t even get into defensive miscues from missed tackles or over-pursuits. 4. The offensive line may have had its worst game Houston was more physically dominating than Fresno State, but that’s to be expected. Oregon State’s offensive line had a brutal showing nearly across the board, with sacks allowed by multiple players in one-on-one matchups. OSU’s rushing stats are skewed by the sacks and not nearly as poor as the final box score, but the bottom line is Fresno State won the line of scrimmage and it’s not a particularly stout group. 5. Josiah Freeman was the best receiver on the field Fresno State’s 6-foot-4 receiver had a big night with two touchdowns. Freeman had a massive advantage against Isaiah Houi and performed accordingly. If there’s one piece OSU’s receiving corps is missing it is a target with the size and length of Freeman, which the Beavers are leaning on via their tight ends. But an outside target like him is hard to beat and he showed why. 6. Tackling, leverage issues persist OSU showed a vulnerability early, but against Houston and Texas Tech it was understandable in terms of talent and timing on the schedule. Tackling improved over the prior five games, but opponents’ speed also dropped. Against legitimate athletic threats, the Beavers showed their tackling fundamentals, speed, strength and angles are still areas of weakness. 7. The areas for Braden Atkinson to develop are clear Entz detailed Atkinson’s reliance on his first read and susceptibility to being impacted by pass rush when it’s not there. Of course, a defense has to have the talent and ability to do something about it. Atkinson’s ceiling is high provided he develops in his reading of progressions, grows more comfortable checking into run plays and finds effective counters to the better defenses OSU faces. 8. Caleb Ojeda came up big Ojeda’s three field goals should not get lost to the box score, particularly with a 54-yarder. At 14-9, if OSU manages to make a stop and gain momentum, the game could have changed and the importance of Ojeda’s kicks becomes paramount to the game. 9. Kickoff coverage remains a problem As the sample size for OSU’s kickoffs grows, so too does the success opponents continue to have. To allow a 44-yard kickoff return following a 14-play drive that spanned more than five minutes is inexcusable. OSU would literally have been better off kicking out of bounds, which has been enough of an issue as well. The Beavers rank 114th in average kickoff return yards allowed and 126th on a per game basis. 10. The weakness at corner is glaring Without belaboring a point that’s been stated on nearly a weekly basis, the matchup disadvantage at No. 2 corner remains the Achilles’ heel for the defense. Against bigger receivers like Freeman it’s simply a matter of when, not if, they will haul in big catches. Read the original article on oregonlive.com . item.title: How Oregon State turned a raw athlete into a starting linebacker
item.description: CORVALLIS — Two years ago, Jarrel Comer was a freshman at Tallahassee Community College and had not played competitive football since middle school. Now he’s a starting outside linebacker at Oregon State . Comer played basketball at Eastside High School in Gainesville, Florida, but began college as a regular student. He looked for opportunities to play sports again and football became the opportunity at Citrus College in California. He boarded a plane for the first time to take a cross-country flight to play football for the first time in more than four years. “I was willing to take that chance to get to where I am today,” Comer said. He had 58 tackles (8.5 for loss), including six sacks at the California junior college and got on the radar of linebackers coach Cort Dennison, then at Idaho. Dennison kept pursuing Comer at OSU, where he signed in January and arrived during the spring. Latest Beavers news Justin Joyner wins first game as Oregon State coach in blowout Atkinson, Legree join Nike’s Blue Ribbon Elite as OSU extends apparel deal Pac-12 confirms play clock error led to penalty on Oregon State in its loss to Fresno State At 6-foot-4 and 245 pounds, Comer was dominating in junior college from his athleticism alone. He didn’t know the finer points of playing football. Hand placement, setting the edge in the run game and pass coverage were not in his repertoire. Comer was there to pin his ears back and attack the quarterback, regardless of the down and distance. “They didn’t ask much of me,” Comer said. “They told me just do what I do, use my athleticism, get to the quarterback.” What Comer lacks in experience, he makes up for in ability. He consistently ranks among OSU’s fastest players in practice, which was invaluable to a team seeking more pass rush. “His athleticism is off the charts,” defensive coordinator Mike MacIntyre said. “We see him grow leaps and bounds. Playing a lot more (against Montana), he will grow leaps and bounds going into this Saturday because now he’s seen it, it slows down, he understands the different things.” RELATED: Experts release Oregon State vs. UTEP predictions, best bets, and preview for Week 4 Comer has 10 tackles thus far, including four in each of the past two games, and is already more than a situational pass rusher for the Beavers. He credits MacIntyre and edge coaches Joe Seumalo and George Frazier with helping him learn the game, particularly pass coverage. Ideally, pairing Comer with Takari Hickle will allow OSU to generate more pressure as teams won’t be able to focus all their offensive line on one side. “Teams have to respect his speed,” Hickle said. “If they don’t, then he’ll run right by them. item.title: Caitlin Clark picks what was ‘the best part’ about the WNBA Finals series
item.description: Photo by Brian Spurlock/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images Indiana Fever star Caitlin Clark thinks that the Golden State Valkyries being in the WNBA Finals was the best part of the series. The Valkyries became the first expansion team in American pro sports history to win a championship in their second year. They achieved this feat by beating the Atlanta Dream in a gruelling seven-game series, which they sealed with a 68-63 win in Game 7. Gabby Williams won the Finals MVP award, as she put on a 30-point performance in Game 7. However, the likes of Kiah Stokes and Veronica Burton also played vital roles in helping the Valkyries beat the Dream. While discussing the WNBA Finals, Caitlin Clark offered major praise for how the Valkyries managed to do what many thought was unthinkable. Caitlin Clark praises Golden State Valkyries team chemistry The Valkyries made the playoffs in their very first WNBA season. However, many were not convinced about them, as they felt that the team lacked the star presence that was required to win the WNBA championship. Gabby Williams made sure to bring this point up after the Game 7 win. The togetherness of the team showed that they were ready to do whatever it takes to win, and Clark had nothing but praise for them. “I feel like the best part about the Finals has been that the Valkyries are in it. They’ve been a franchise for two years. I don’t think people realise how ridiculous that is, that they’ve been able to put together a roster and run an organisation as well as they have,” said Clark on Not Gonna Lie with Kylie Kelce. “For Natalie, their coach, to get everybody to buy in, and to get everybody to believe, and they have really talented players but at the same time, on any given night, any of them can have 20 points and be the star. It seems like nobody’s bothered by that, that’s just how they are. They’re a close-knit team. That’s the coolest storyline of the Finals.” No player on the Valkyries roster averaged 15 or more points in the 2026 season. Chicago Sky and Connecticut Sun were the only two teams to have a similar stat. Both of these teams failed to make the playoffs, while the Valkyries marched on to win the championship. The key reason behind this is that all the players on the Valkyries knew their roles and fulfilled them to their best potential. Williams, who was the star of the Finals, had several off games even against the Dream, but other players stepped up and made the difference. Game 5 was a perfect example of that, as Williams struggled and scored 9 points while shooting 3-for-14 from the field. Burton stepped up to add 13 points, 8 rebounds and also had 4 blocks to help the Valkyries get to a 64-55 win. There were multiple games during the season that their bench won them. They had the best bench unit during the regular season, which averaged 34.3 points per game. item.title: Marcus Smart Proves He Still Owns The Celtics
item.description: Troy Taormina-Imagn Images There is a reason the Celtics lost their five-game winning streak on Monday night, and the answer wears a Rockets jersey. Marcus Smart did exactly what he always does: he got under the skin of his former team and turned a close game into a blowout. The final score of 109-93 tells one story, but the real tale is in the chaos Smart unleashed. He made Boston pay for every mistake with a mix of defense and dirty talk that only he can pull off. item.title: Yankees' David Bednar projected to get a 'slightly better' contract than Devin Williams
item.description: Yankees' David Bednar projected to get a 'slightly better' contract than Devin Williams originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The New York Yankees have some very interesting decisions to make this offseason, with the Trent Grisham, Jazz Chisholm Jr., and David Bednar decisions being the headliners. But of those three, the one they're most likely to bring back is Bednar, especially after they placed the qualifying offer on him and didn't do so for Chisholm or Grisham. When it comes to Bednar, however, keeping him might prove tricky. The reason is that ESPN's Kiley McDaniel is projecting that Bednar will get a "slightly better" contract than what Devin Williams got last year, a deal in which the Yankees didn't match. David Bednar projected to get a better contract than Devin Williams did last offseason. "11. David Bednar, RHRP... Projected contract/QO: three years, $60 million (20 AAV), received QB," McDaniel writes. "... He has a slightly better case than Devin Williams, who landed a three-year, $51 million deal with deferrals last winter, so I have Bednar a notch above that." The Yankees' right-handed reliever is slated to earn quite a lot of money this offseason, with the Yankees already putting over $20 million on the table by extending him the qualifying offer. But if Bednar can reach this projected contract from McDaniel, coming in at $20 million per year over three years for a total of $60 million, then he'll likely decline the qualifying offer and sign a strong deal this November. MORE : Yankees predicted to sign 39-HR Triple Crown winner to replace disappointing Ryan McMahon Bednar is 32 years old, so a long-term deal beyond three years isn't likely, especially since he's a reliever. But with 143 saves over the past five seasons and a strong pitch combo with his fastball and splitter, Bednar is likely to land a strong deal this offseason. McDaniel is predicting it'll come in better than what Williams got last offseason. The Yankees let Williams go, as he signed with the New York Mets on that $51 million deal. If the Yankees aren't willing to pay top dollar for a reliever, Bednar might be gone too. However, with Chisholm and Grisham seemingly on their way out this offseason, re-signing Bednar might be more in play than Williams was a year ago. item.title: Gafford’s Elite Rim Protection Exposes Dallas’ Three-Point Woes
item.description: Jerome Miron-Imagn Images Daniel Gafford is the best rim protector in the entire NBA, yet the Dallas Mavericks still look shaky on defense. Opponents fall 22.1 percentage points short of their expected basket field goal rate when he defends them. That stat is huge, but per The Smoking Cuban , the team’s overall defense is just so-so at best. Gafford is doing his job, but the system around him has a fatal flaw that needs fixing now. The problem is that Dallas is betting its season on opponents missing open shots. Despite Gafford’s elite metrics, the Mavericks have shown only so-so defensive performance. Beyond the arc, opponents shoot 29.7 percent, a mark ranking 29th in the league. That number looks great right now, but it is not a sustainable plan for a championship run. If the league starts hitting those open looks, Dallas will crumble fast. The Danger of Open Threes Look at the deeper numbers and the worry gets real. Per The Smoking Cuban , opponents are shooting 26.6 percent on open 3-pointers, which is 30th in the NBA. This number sits almost eight percentage points under the league median. Put differently, teams would net roughly one extra 3-pointer per game hitting at an average clip. One extra shot per game changes the outcome of close contests, and Dallas cannot rely on bad luck forever. Worse yet, the Mavs are not forcing enough turnovers to create easy points. Mavericks opponents are coughing it up 15.0 times per game, ranking 23rd in the NBA. While Dallas ranks 14th in points off turnovers, the lack of pressure means the defense is just sitting back. They are not disrupting the flow, and they are letting teams get comfortable against a system that depends on Gafford being on the floor every single minute. What Happens When Gafford Sits? With Gafford playing, Dallas performs 21.7 points per 100 possessions better. That gap is insane, but it raises a terrifying question about their rotation. The team has no other bigs who can match his impact. Morez Johnson Jr. and P.J. Washington have not come close to matching that pro-level protection. Johnson is already picking up 3.2 fouls per game in just 15.5 minutes, which limits his time on the floor. If Gafford rests, the rim protection vanishes. This reliance creates a clear ceiling for the team. They need to force more turnovers and stop giving up wide-open looks. The defense has been splashy because of Gafford, Zaccharie Risacher, and Cooper Flagg, but the point of attack is still slipping. A defensive rating of 111.3 places Dallas 16th in the league, right in the middle of the pack.

item.title: LeBron James Sips Fan’s Wine After Crash In 76ers Win
item.description: Bill Streicher-Imagn Images LeBron James did not just crash into a Philadelphia 76ers fan on Monday night; he actually tasted the wine the fan was holding. The star player took a sip of the spilled drink after a fastbreak collision, then told reporters he wanted to see “how good it was.” This unusual moment happened during the 76ers’ 126-107 win over the Chicago Bulls, a game that marked their fourth straight victory. James admitted the contact was messy but kept the mood light. After recording 15 points, nine assists, and seven rebounds, “I crashed into him, spilled some of his wine,” James said. He did not stop there. “So I wanted to see if it was worth it on my arm and how good it was. It was alright.” Laughter filled the room as he shared the story, showing the relaxed vibe around the team right now. A Long Season Needs Fun The 76ers have won seven of their first eight games, sitting at the top of the Eastern Conference. That kind of success often brings serious pressure, but James argues that players need to find joy to survive the grind. “It’s a long marathon, and if you don’t find ways to have fun throughout — even though you’re working, even though you’re locked in — it can wear on you,” James said. Joel Embiid and Tyrese Maxey started alongside James, while VJ Edgecombe and Jaylen Brown also took the floor for the opening tip. Every starter scored in double-figures, with Maxey leading the charge with 26 points. The team’s chemistry looks sharp, and the players seem to be enjoying the process rather than just the result. Associated Press noted that the win improved the team’s record to 7-1. Why the Sip Matters Fans in Philadelphia have seen their share of heartbreak, so seeing a player like James share a laugh with a supporter feels different. It breaks the wall between the court and the stands. ESPN reported that fans are still talking about the moment, calling it a wild sight to see during a live game. TheScore confirmed the event, noting that James drank from the fan’s cup right after the collision. Yahoo Sports added that NBA fans across the league could not believe what they saw on the broadcast. The moment was not planned, yet it fits the current narrative of a 76ers team that is winning while keeping things fresh. When a player performs at this level and still finds time to joke about a spilled drink, it signals a team that is comfortable in its own skin. The 76ers will need to keep this energy as the season moves forward.

item.title: West Ham eye Parker move after sacking Nuno
item.description: Scott Parker has been linked with the West Ham manager's job (Paul ELLIS) West Ham are expected to hire Scott Parker as their new manager after the Championship club sacked Nuno Espirito Santo on Tuesday. Parker is believed to be West Ham's top choice to replace Nuno and could be appointed in time for Wednesday's match against Cardiff after opening talks with the club. The former England midfielder spent four seasons as a player with West Ham and led Bournemouth and Burnley to promotion from the Championship as a manager. Parker, 46, also had spells in charge at Fulham and Club Brugge. West Ham are looking for their fourth permanent boss since David Moyes left in May 2024. Julen Lopetegui was sacked after just six months in charge and Graham Potter was axed after only eight months in charge. Nuno, 52, oversaw the Hammers' relegation from the Premier League last season but stayed with the east London club in a bid to lead them back into the top flight. Many viewed the Hammers as favourites to win automatic promotion, but they are currently eighth in the second-tier table, six points behind leaders Middlesbrough, after 13 games. West Ham had lost their past two league games against Southampton and West Brom. Nuno, who previously managed Wolves, Tottenham and Nottingham Forest, was appointed in September last year. "West Ham United can confirm that men's first-team head coach Nuno Espirito Santo has left his position with immediate effect," the club said in a statement. "Following a thorough review of the start to the EFL Championship season, the board of directors believe that a change is necessary at this time in order to ensure that the club's objectives and expectations remain on track." jw-smg/jc

item.title: Netflix Reportedly Working on Dana White Documentary Set For Early 2027 Release
item.description: USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect Netflix did not land the UFC, but it is still getting a project centered on Dana White . According to Page Six , Netflix was close enough to securing the rights to stream UFC events in 2025 that it approved a White documentary to go along with the fights. The UFC deal never happened, but production continued, and Page Six reports the film will likely debut in the first three months of 2027. The film is directed by Gotham Chopra, a co-founder of Religion of Sports, whose credits include the Tom Brady docuseries Tom vs Time and Man in the Arena. Chopra declined to comment to Page Six. The project started as a documentary about Las Vegas before shifting its focus to White. That appears to match a November 2025 report from The Hollywood Reporter, which said Netflix was developing an unscripted project about White’s gambling in Las Vegas casinos. The documentary now centers on White, 57, who persuaded Frank and Lorenzo Fertitta to spend $2 million on the UFC in 2001. Fifteen years later, a group led by Endeavor, then known as WME-IMG, paid $4 billion for the company. The documentary was greenlit by Bela Bajaria, who left her role as Netflix’s chief content officer in October 2026, with Peter Rice named as her replacement. Netflix’s pursuit of the UFC fell apart over the size of the package. TKO president Mark Shapiro said on Puck’s The Varsity podcast in September 2025 that talks with Netflix were close, but the streamer “didn’t want to have the volume.” Netflix was interested in the UFC’s numbered events, while TKO wanted them bundled with its Fight Night cards. “And that’s what opened the door for Paramount and CBS,” Shapiro said. Credit: Jasmin Frank-USA TODAY Sports Paramount announced a seven-year, $7.7 billion deal for exclusive U.S. rights to the UFC in August 2025. The agreement started in 2026 and moved the promotion away from its long-running pay-per-view model, with every event streaming on Paramount+ and select numbered cards simulcast on CBS. Chopra will have no shortage of material from 2026. In June, the UFC held UFC Freedom 250 on the South Lawn of the White House, where Justin Gaethje beat Ilia Topuria for the undisputed lightweight title and Ciryl Gane stopped Alex Pereira to win the interim heavyweight title. White has also spent 2026 building Zuffa Boxing, the promotion he launched with Turki Alalshikh, the chairman of Saudi Arabia’s General Entertainment Authority. The company’s first event under its Paramount partnership took place in January, and it has since run cards in the United States, England and Ireland. Missing out on the UFC did not end Netflix’s business with White and TKO. The streamer has carried WWE Raw since January 2025 through its deal with TKO, the same parent company that owns the UFC, and it streamed the Canelo Alvarez vs. Terence Crawford fight that served as the first Zuffa Boxing event in September 2025. A documentary on White keeps that connection going, even without U

item.title: LeBron James reveals major reason behind early-season injuries
item.description: The 2026-27 NBA season has already brought several injury setbacks for some of the league’s biggest names. Teams are losing key players early in the campaign, with some facing lengthy spells on the sidelines. Philadelphia 76ers star LeBron James has shared his thoughts on the growing injury concerns. He believes the pace of today’s game is making it increasingly difficult for players to prepare for the physical demands of the regular season. His comments offer a different perspective on the challenges players face when transitioning from offseason preparation to regular-season competition. MORE: Insane LeBron James stat gives 76ers real NBA Finals hope LeBron James points to NBA’s pace as a factor behind early-season injuries Philadelphia 76ers forward LeBron James. Mandatory Credit: Trevor Ruszkowski-Imagn Images Speaking on the Mind the Game podcast, James discussed the injuries affecting several players at the start of the 2026-27 season, including Anthony Edwards and Tyrese Haliburton . “We go back to the pace of the game right now and I think it has a lot to do with it. There’s no way that you can simulate the way we’re playing in today’s game, to offseason training,” James said. item.title: Islanders sign Stanley Cup-winning defenseman to professional tryout
item.description: Stephen R. Sylvanie-Imagn Images Islanders sign Stanley Cup-winning defenseman to professional tryout appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The New York Islanders are decimated on the blue line, with Alexander Romanov likely out for the season with a torn ACL and Ryan Pulock recently joining him on the shelf with an upper-body injury. Although the Isles still have a relatively strong defensive unit, led by budding franchise cornerstone Matthew Schaefer , the team brought in some extra help earlier this week. New York signed Ben Hutton to a professional tryout (PTO) contract on Monday, general manager Mathieu Darche announced. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) The tryout allows Hutton to practice with the Islanders, but he’ll need a standard NHL contract before appearing in a regular-season game. Hutton, who was part of the Vegas Golden Knights’ 2023 Stanley Cup-winning team, recorded six goals and 15 points in 55 games with the Knights in 2025-26. It was a career high in goals for the 33-year-old, who again helped Vegas reach the Stanley Cup Final in the spring, where it lost to Carolina in six games. Hutton appeared in seven games during the run, chipping in an assist. He turned a one-year deal with the Knights back in 2021 into a five-year stint with the team, which saw him appear in 10 postseason contests. The veteran rearguard had a PTO with the Ottawa Senators during the preseason but was unable to turn that into a standard contract ahead of the 2026-27 campaign. Originally selected by the Vancouver Canucks in the fifth round of the 2012 NHL Draft, Hutton spent the first four seasons of his career in British Columbia, although the team failed to advance to the Stanley Cup Playoffs during his tenure. He ended up signing a one-year contract with the Los Angeles Kings in 2019 and also played for the Anaheim Ducks and Toronto Maple Leafs. Over 11 National Hockey League seasons split between the Canucks, Kings, Ducks, Leafs and Golden Knights, the Brockville, Ontario native has accumulated 30 goals and 139 points in 575 regular-season games. Before he turned professional, Hutton enjoyed three productive seasons as a University of Maine Black Bear, recording 65 points in 108 contests from 2012 to 2015. It’ll be interesting to see if he can earn himself a contract for the rest of the campaign on an injury-riddled New York blue line. The Islanders, who are 7-5-2 and in third place in the Metropolitan Division, are back in action against the defending Stanley Cup champion Hurricanes on Thursday night.

item.title: Giants Fans Can Stream The Eagles Game On A Phone Without Cable
item.description: Thomas Shea-Imagn Images Giants fans can watch the game on Sunday without a cable subscription. Per Giants.com , the entire matchup between the New York Giants and the Philadelphia Eagles can be streamed directly on a mobile phone through NFL+. This service lets fans catch every snap from Lincoln Financial Field on Sunday, November 8, without paying for a traditional TV package. While the TV broadcast airs on FOX at 1:00 p.m. ET, the radio experience offers a different kind of access for those on the go. Bob Papa leads the play-by-play duties alongside analyst Carl Banks and sideline reporter Howard Cross on WFAN 101.9 FM and 660 AM. The station begins its coverage with “Giants Gameday” at 11:00 a.m., presented by Hackensack Meridian Health, and provides fans with more than two hours of pre‑game analysis before kickoff.11:00 am, presented by Hackensack Meridian Health, giving fans two hours of pre‑game analysis before kickoff. Radio Reach Extends Far Beyond New York For fans living outside the immediate New York market, the Giants Radio Network ensures no one misses a play. The network lists dozens of affiliates across the region, including WPYX 106.5 FM in Albany and 96.3 FM “The Buzzer” in Cortland and Ithaca. Fans in Hartford can tune into WPOP 1410 AM, while listeners in Easton, PA, have access to WEEX 1230 AM and 94.7 FM. The reach stretches even further into upstate New York and Connecticut with stations like WTLA 1200 AM in Syracuse and WLAD 800 AM in Danbury. Spanish-speaking fans can catch the action on Que Buena 1280 AM, where Nestor Rosario handles play-by-play and Francis Adames provides analysis. This wide network means a fan in Rome, NY, or Binghamton, NY, can hear the same calls as someone sitting in the MetLife Stadium parking lot. Postgame Coverage Starts Immediately Once the final whistle blows, the broadcast team does not just sign off. Giants Postgame Live, presented by Hackensack Meridian Health, begins right after the game ends. Hosted by Michelle Gingras, this show airs on MSG Networks, the DAZN App, YouTube, and the official Giants platforms. For those who prefer a deeper dive into the stats and highlights, the “Giants Extra Point” show presented by Earth Treasures Fine Jewelers offers extended coverage. The official Giants mobile app and GiantsTV video streaming app also serve as central hubs for replays and big plays. Fans can follow the team on Instagram, Twitter, and TikTok for live updates that happen in real time during the contest. SiriusXM subscribers have another option available on channel 267 for the radio broadcast and channel 823 for the streaming feed. The rivalry between these two teams runs deep, and the Giants.com photo gallery even highlights rare historical moments from past clashes. From Steve Filipowicz’s interception in 1946 to Kyle Rote’s incomplete pass in 1961., the history is always part of the story. The game on November 8 marks a key moment in the season for both clubs. item.title: What will 'exciting' McNamara bring to Leinster?
item.description: After much speculation, Noel McNamara has been handed the keys at Leinster to replace outgoing head coach Leo Cullen. McNamara is currently attacking coach at Bordeaux Begles, and helped to mastermind a dominating victory over Leinster in the Investec Champions Cup final in May. When he was announced, McNamara described the Leinster job as "one of the most prestigious roles in world rugby". But what will the 43-year-old bring to the Irish province when he takes over next year? Ireland full-back Hugo Keenen has a long-standing relationship with McNamara, which goes back to when he was playing for UCD in the All-Ireland League, and he said it was "great news". McNamara to succeed Cullen as Leinster head coach The pair would have more interactions at Leinster when McNamara was working at the province as academy manager and Leinster A's head coach. After five years in Dublin, where he also coached Ireland's Under-20s to Grand Slam success in 2019, McNamara made the move to South Africa in 2021 to join the Sharks as attack and backs coach. From there, he joined Bordeaux in 2023 and has helped the French side to back-to-back European titles. Keenan, who is in Ireland camp ahead of November's Nations Championship matches, said it was "an exciting appointment". "It's good to have him on board and I think that's the general feedback amongst the squad," Keenan said. "I'm sure he's got a different perspective of things, by getting out of the building, going down to South Africa, challenging himself down there, and going so well and thriving at Bordeaux." 'Presence in a room' Leinster know first hand what a McNamara-led attack can do, which was evident in the Champions Cup final in May. The Irish province had no answer to Bordeaux in Bilbao as the French outfit made it consecutive European crowns with a crushing 41-19 win. After that win, McNamara told BBC Sport he had used Rory McIlroy, who had not long won back-to-back at the Masters, as motivation for his players. McNamara had also spoken about Leinster's character in bouncing back after so many defeats, and said "tough times create tough people". "Obviously, we know what he's achieved at Bordeaux and he's been on the better side of a few results than us recently," Keenan added. "You see what their backline and attacks have been producing, and I suppose that's his fingerprint on it. "I'm excited to see what he has and to work with him. I think it's positive for me and everyone at Leinster." Keenan added that the departing Cullen was "big boots to fill" after a trophy-laden 12 years with Leinster. item.title: After rocky exhibitions, Northwestern found some answers
item.description: Two exhibition losses left Northwestern with more questions than answers. After a 94-59 loss to Iowa State, the Wildcats spent the last week trying to fix what went wrong. On Monday night, they showed they made some progress. NU opened the regular season with an 86-60 win over Binghamton in a game it never trailed. The ‘Cats shot 55.8% from the field, including 72% in the first half, and stayed true to the Northwestern way, committing just eight turnovers. This comes just two weeks after the Wildcats committed 20 turnovers against Illinois State and shot 32.8% against Iowa State. “We just talked about it; none of those stats matter at the end of the day,” Collins said after the game. “I thought our guys came out and had great energy. Thought we played with great confidence.” Collins said postgame that he and his staff had spent the week working out the kinks in the defense and added more offensive sets to help put the ball in the right hands. The results showed that, as the Wildcats got out in transition after stops, kept the ball moving and made it difficult for Binghamton to find good shots. The ‘Cats dished out 23 assists in the win and had 18 points off of 12 Bearcat turnovers, and outscored them in transition, 14-2. “23 assists, eight turnovers,” Collins said. “That’s Northwestern basketball.” As in the exhibition games, the offense once again ran through sophomore Jake West, who finished just one assist shy of his career-high at 12, while adding 20 points on 6-for-9 shooting and going 6-for-6 from the line. Most of that production came in the first half, when he had 14 points and eight assists, working off of ball screens. Collins praised West for how Northwestern had finished last season and carried that into the offseason. Collins said West has grown from the quiet voice he was in his freshman year into one of the team’s most vocal leaders, alongside junior Angelo Ciaravino, who make up two-thirds of the returners, along with sophomore Phoenix Gill. Collins compared West’s value to the impact quarterback Aidan Chiles has on Northwestern football next door at Ryan Field. “You guys are seeing it. Our football team, right? When you have a great quarterback, you have a chance, and that’s no different than in basketball,” Collins said. “When that position is in a good spot, you have poise, you have leadership, and you have a guy making good decisions.” Collins said it was Northwestern’s first 20-point, 10-assist game since Bryant McIntosh, the legendary former Wildcats point guard and current assistant coach. item.content:encoded: Two exhibition losses left Northwestern with more questions than answers. After a 94-59 loss to Iowa State, the Wildcats spent the last week trying to fix what went wrong. On Monday night, they showed they made some progress. NU opened the regular season with an 86-60 win over Binghamton in a game it never trailed. The ‘Cats shot 55.8% from the field, including 72% in the first half, and stayed true to the Northwestern way, committing just eight turnovers. This comes just two weeks after the Wildcats committed 20 turnovers against Illinois State and shot 32.8% against Iowa State. “We just talked about it; none of those stats matter at the end of the day,” Collins said after the game. “I thought our guys came out and had great energy. Thought we played with great confidence.” Collins said postgame that he and his staff had spent the week working out the kinks in the defense and added more offensive sets to help put the ball in the right hands. The results showed that, as the Wildcats got out in transition after stops, kept the ball moving and made it difficult for Binghamton to find good shots. The ‘Cats dished out 23 assists in the win and had 18 points off of 12 Bearcat turnovers, and outscored them in transition, 14-2. “23 assists, eight turnovers,” Collins said. “That’s Northwestern basketball.” As in the exhibition games, the offense once again ran through sophomore Jake West, who finished just one assist shy of his career-high at 12, while adding 20 points on 6-for-9 shooting and going 6-for-6 from the line. Most of that production came in the first half, when he had 14 points and eight assists, working off of ball screens. Collins praised West for how Northwestern had finished last season and carried that into the offseason. Collins said West has grown from the quiet voice he was in his freshman year into one of the team’s most vocal leaders, alongside junior Angelo Ciaravino, who make up two-thirds of the returners, along with sophomore Phoenix Gill. Collins compared West’s value to the impact quarterback Aidan Chiles has on Northwestern football next door at Ryan Field. “You guys are seeing it. Our football team, right? When you have a great quarterback, you have a chance, and that’s no different than in basketball,” Collins said. “When that position is in a good spot, you have poise, you have leadership, and you have a guy making good decisions.” Collins said it was Northwestern’s first 20-point, 10-assist game since Bryant McIntosh, the legendary former Wildcats point guard and current assistant coach. West let him hear it in the locker room, joking that McIntosh subbed him out because “he knew how many assists I had.” Of those 12 assists, five went to graduate transfer Jack Karasinski, including four of his seven made threes that night. He finished with a team-high 24 points on 8-for-12 shooting and 7-for-11 from deep, and was the first Wildcat to hit seven threes since Ty Berry did so two years ago. “I like to say I have delusional confidence out there,” Karasinski said. “Once I touch it, it’s going up.” That was prevalent in the game. After airballing a three in the second half, Karasinski showed short-term memory, coming right back down the floor and firing a three from well behind the arc, which fell true on his second attempt. Graduate transfer LA Pratt showed that too. Pratt had struggled in the two exhibition games, including going 1-for-7 from the field and having five turnovers against Illinois State. After the misses, Pratt’s shot started to fall. “I kind of saw, let the air out of the balloon and kind of got him going,” Collins said. Pratt finished the game with 19 points on 6-for-12 shooting, including a big three with time dwindling at the end of the first half, when he pulled up from deep to put Northwestern up 51-35 at the break. The program also made a shocking announcement just over an hour before tip-off that the Wildcats would be without fourth-year big man Luke McEldon, who is taking a leave of absence from the program for an “indefinite” time. Collins confirmed postgame and declined to share more details out of respect for his privacy. Without McEldon, who started the two exhibition games, junior Okku Federiko took over at center — a position he doesn’t typically play — and kept the team afloat in his 23 minutes, finishing plus-20 in that time. The problems were still there. The second half was less tidy, with the team shooting 41% and going 5-for-18 from deep. Bench production also left much to be desired, with the reserves combining for just six points. Collins said he’s trying to figure it all out on the fly. “We’re such a work in progress,” Collins said. “I’m learning these guys. We’ve already made a number of adjustments even since we started playing exhibition games.” The win gives them a nice confidence boost, but one good night doesn’t settle every question raised in October. But just a week after Collins told his team their season would be defined by how they responded, the Wildcats responded well. They’ll look to build on that in the non-conference schedule, when they play host to Stony Brook this Friday, Nov. 6, at 7 p.m. CST.

item.title: Jon Rahm’s Brutal Truth About LIV Golf’s Failed Pivot
item.description: Jerod Ringwald-Imagn Images Jon Rahm walked away from LIV Golf’s next phase because the new direction felt wrong to him. He told reporters at the Abu Dhabi Aldar Championship that he “wasn’t thrilled” with the changes proposed for LIV 2.0. The 31-year-old Spaniard decided the future plan lacked the special team elements that defined the original project. His departure signals a clear break from a league trying to restructure after losing its main financial backer. Why The New Plan Failed To Impress Rahm liked the initial concept of the league but drew a hard line at the new proposals. He stated at a press conference, “As much as I liked the project and the idea on, let’s say, LIV 1.0, I wasn’t thrilled with the changes they were doing to 2.0 and I just wasn’t willing to follow that path.” The league is now attempting a relaunch after Saudi Arabia’s Public Investment Fund pulled its support. This move required the company to file for Chapter 11 bankruptcy and cancel existing player contracts. Rahm gave up claims against the bankruptcy estate, reported to be worth up to $150 million, but kept his team’s intellectual property. He simply did not see the value in the new model. The former world number one felt the new proposals drifted too far from team golf. He noted, “It wasn’t anything special, anything that stood out. I just didn’t like what they were going with 2.0.” There were too many unknowns for him to commit. The structure seemed to shift toward a regular tournament format rather than the team competition that attracted players initially. Rahm called the new approach “more of a regular tournament” and said it “wasn’t really ever much of a consideration.” The Road Back To The DP World Tour With the LIV door closed, Rahm is focusing on his return to the DP World Tour. He is set to play at the Abu Dhabi Aldar Championship this week. He admitted he is currently “rusty” after a long flight and a break from practice. Their daughter Begona was expected by his wife Kelley, necessitating the break. His current standing on the Race to Dubai rankings sits at 51st. He faces a potential one-year suspension if he wishes to return to the PGA Tour. He acknowledged that Brooks Koepka managed to return through specific circumstances, but Rahm remains unsure if those same doors will open for him. He said, “Obviously, Brooks was able to go back through certain circumstances.” If a suspension is required, he views it as a chance to play on the DP World Tour for a year. He added, “But if I have to fulfil a one-year suspension, I think it’s a pretty good position to be that a worst-case scenario I get to play on a wonderful tour (DP World Tour) for a whole year.” A Final Look At The Deal Rahm is realistic about the financial terms he might face compared to other players. The 31-year-old Spaniard decided the future plan lacked the special team elements that defined the original project. His departure signals a clear break from a league trying to restructure after losing its main financial backer. Why The New Plan Failed To Impress Rahm liked the initial concept of the league but drew a hard line at the new proposals. He stated at a press conference, “As much as I liked the project and the idea on, let’s say, LIV 1.0, I wasn’t thrilled with the changes they were doing to 2.0 and I just wasn’t willing to follow that path.” The league is now attempting a relaunch after Saudi Arabia’s Public Investment Fund pulled its support. This move required the company to file for Chapter 11 bankruptcy and cancel existing player contracts. Rahm gave up claims against the bankruptcy estate, reported to be worth up to $150 million, but kept his team’s intellectual property. He simply did not see the value in the new model. The former world number one felt the new proposals drifted too far from team golf. He noted, “It wasn’t anything special, anything that stood out. I just didn’t like what they were going with 2.0.” There were too many unknowns for him to commit. The structure seemed to shift toward a regular tournament format rather than the team competition that attracted players initially. Rahm called the new approach “more of a regular tournament” and said it “wasn’t really ever much of a consideration.” The Road Back To The DP World Tour With the LIV door closed, Rahm is focusing on his return to the DP World Tour. He is set to play at the Abu Dhabi Aldar Championship this week. He admitted he is currently “rusty” after a long flight and a break from practice. Their daughter Begona was expected by his wife Kelley, necessitating the break. His current standing on the Race to Dubai rankings sits at 51st. He faces a potential one-year suspension if he wishes to return to the PGA Tour. He acknowledged that Brooks Koepka managed to return through specific circumstances, but Rahm remains unsure if those same doors will open for him. He said, “Obviously, Brooks was able to go back through certain circumstances.” If a suspension is required, he views it as a chance to play on the DP World Tour for a year. He added, “But if I have to fulfil a one-year suspension, I think it’s a pretty good position to be that a worst-case scenario I get to play on a wonderful tour (DP World Tour) for a whole year.” A Final Look At The Deal Rahm is realistic about the financial terms he might face compared to other players. He doubts he will get the same deal as Brooks Koepka, which included a five million US dollar charitable donation. He stated, “I seriously doubt I get offered the same deal that Brooks did, but if I got offered exactly the same penalties as him (stringent restrictions on his financial benefits and a charitable donation of five million US dollars), I probably would do it, yes.” The Independent reported these details regarding his press conference comments. This honesty shows a player who values the game over a check that no longer fits his vision.

item.title: LeBron James Sips Wine While Sixers Crush Bulls
item.description: Bill Streicher-Imagn Images LeBron James is averaging his lowest scoring numbers ever at 16.4 points, yet he helped lead Philadelphia to a dominant 126-107 win over the Chicago Bulls on Monday night. The 41-year-old star is shooting just 45 percent from the field, a stat that looks rough on paper but didn’t stop the Sixers from securing their fourth straight victory. While the stats show a dip in his usual scoring output, the game showed a different side of the legend in action. A Viral Sip and a Massive Dunk The most talked-about moment didn’t come from a bucket but from behind the basket where James grabbed a cup from a fan named Troy Clemens. According to Heavy.com , the season-ticket holder offered the star some wine and James reportedly took a sip during the second minute of the contest. This viral clip spread across social media quickly, showing a rare, relaxed moment for the veteran leader. An emphatic double-pump jam by James, occurring just before that interaction, netted the 76ers’ first field goal of the game. That powerful dunk came less than two minutes into the action, proving he still has explosive power despite his age. James is set to turn 42 years old in just under two months, making his current performance even more impressive for many observers. Tyrese Maxey, Joel Embiid, and Jaylen Brown now shoulder most scoring duties as his significantly altered role requires deferring to them. This change has allowed him to focus more on defense, where his lesser involvement on offense has freed him up to be a force on the other end of the floor. He is averaging 7.0 rebounds and 7.0 assists per contest, showing he still controls the game without needing to be the primary scorer. Edgecombe’s Perfect Half and a Broken Defense Edgecombe finished the first half a perfect 7-of-7 from the field, including one catch-and-shoot three-pointer that added to his impressive night. He turned into the Sixers’ version of a deep threat, running go routes that the Bulls either could not or would not stop for 15 first-half points. This defensive breakdown allowed Philadelphia to coast to a 126-107 win, as reported by PHLY Sports . Because James and Maxey distributed the ball well as passers, three 76ers players scored 20 or more points in the game. Maxey led the team with 26 points and racked up seven assists in the first half alone to match LeBron. The team’s biggest star has taken on a less scoring‑heavy role. The Bulls will need to tighten up their transition defense if they hope to stop this balanced Philadelphia offense in future matchups.
