item.title: Francesco Bagnaia counting down days until end of Ducati MotoGP tenure
item.description: Motorsport photo Francesco Bagnaia says the last three rounds of the 2026 MotoGP struggles will be about “surviving”, with no solution in sight for his ongoing issues with Ducati’s GP26. The three-time world champion had high hopes from last weekend’s Malaysian Grand Prix, having identified Sepang as his best opportunity to score a big result before leaving the Borgo Panigale marque at the end of the year. Bagnaia had managed to ride through his bike problems at last year’s Malaysian GP to secure pole position and a Sprint victory, giving him confidence that he could perform well again this time around. But after qualifying 10th on the grid and smashing his windscreen in frustration, the Italian could only muster a 13th place result on Sunday, having even slipped outside the points at one stage. Asked whether he was counting the days until the end of the year, Bagnaia replied: “[Yes, but] not just from this moment.” Pressed further as to what he could expect from the final races, with the evidence that the Ducati had failed to work to his liking at one of his favourite tracks, he replied “surviving”. Francesco Bagnaia, Ducati Team Francesco Bagnaia, Ducati Team Bagnaia has been suffering from grip issues since the start of the year, but was still able to secure some headline results in the first half of the season - including four consecutive Sunday podiums and a sprint win at Brno. However, his form nosedived after the summer break, with the last eight rounds yielding a pair of sixth-place sprint finishes as his best results. The 29-year-old said he had been unable to push for even a single lap at Sepang on Sunday, with his performance deteriorating particularly badly in the closing stages of the race. “It looked exactly like I was expecting, no more no less,” he admitted. “On Saturday, I was just lucky that it started to rain. But on Sunday, I saw that my limit was the grip. I tried to manage it. “Even managing it, after five laps I was without the rear tyre and I needed to start thinking about just finishing the race. The last lap I did was 2m05.1s. For me it's something unbelievable, considering what I know that I can do here, that is what it is. “It's like this and we need to accept it. Three to go and try to do the maximum.” Asked how difficult it was to reach the finish on worn tyres, he replied: “It was dead easy, because I wasn't able to do any push lap. It was like doing an easy run.” Bagnaia’s last lap at Sepang - a 2m05.143s - was a full two seconds slower than his team-mate Marc Marquez , who had backed off considerably as he celebrated his seventh grand prix win of the season. Among other Ducati riders, Alex Marquez and Franco Morbidelli were also able to lap within the 2m02s bracket in the closing stages of the race, while Fabio di Giannantonio ’s pace dipped into the mid 2m03s. item.title: New York Post makes Game of Thrones quip as John Harbaugh teases Giants trade deadline bombshell
item.description: New York Post makes Game of Thrones quip as John Harbaugh teases Giants trade deadline bombshell appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . As the NFL trade deadline approaches, John Harbaugh and the New York Giants may be buyers, which resulted in The New York Post making a pun involving Game of Thrones . Today’s issue of The New York Post devoted two pages to the Giants, including rumors involving the trade deadline. Harbaugh said he’d take “any call” about trades before the deadline next week. Giants spread in today’s New York Post. https://t.co/aICaofYRia Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) — Paul Schwartz (@NYPost_Schwartz) November 3, 2026 The piece about the trade deadline is dubbed “Game of Phones.” We’ll see how active Harbaugh’s phone is over the next week or so. Will the Giants make moves at the trade deadline? Vincent Carchietta-Imagn Images The Giants have a week to make any trades before the deadline at 4 pm EST on Nov. 10. There have been rampant rumors about them making moves. While they are 4-2-1 and in first place in the NFC East, the Giants should not be content. They could use some help at the running back position. Cam Skattebo, the team’s starter, was benched in a previous game. Tyrone Tracy Jr. was also placed on injured reserve last week with a hamstring injury. Najee Harris was brought in during the offseason but was cut after making comments about the team’s running back rotation. The team still has Devin Singletary and Greg Desrosiers Jr. on the roster. The Giants are coming off their bye in Week 8. They won an overtime thriller against the Houston Texans before their break. Their next game is against the Philadelphia Eagles, who are reeling after losing Jalen Hurts for the season, in Week 9. Philly has lost seven games in a row after starting the year 2-0. Harbaugh’s tenure with the Giants is off to a hot start. Given the state of the NFC East, they have a good chance to win the division. This comes after Harbaugh’s 18-year career with the Baltimore Ravens, during which he won a Super Bowl. Related: Giants’ John Harbaugh admits calling AFC team as trade deadline looms Related: The reason Giants RB Cam Skattebo was fined $7,073 after Texans game

item.title: Warriors Star Draymond Green Ejected After Fiery Scuffle with Suns’ Dillon Brooks
item.description: Draymond Green and Dillon Brooks on Nov. 2, 2026 Credit: NBA on ESPN/X.com NEED TO KNOW Warriors’ Draymond Green was ejected after he put his hands on Dillon Brooks’ neck on Monday, Nov. 2 Brooks ran up to Green after the Warriors star committed a hard foul on Khaman Maluach, throwing him to the floor Steph Curry said Green’s scuffle with Brooks “lit a fire in” the Warriors, who went on to win 116-113 Draymond Green was ejected from the Golden State Warriors’ matchup against the Phoenix Suns on Monday, Nov. 2 after he and Dillons Brooks got into it in the third quarter. The Warriors were down by seven points when Green, 36, committed a hard foul on Suns center Khaman Maluach, throwing him to the floor on a shot attempt. Maluach, 20, remained on the floor for a moment as an upset Brooks, 30, ran up to Green. Green grabbed Brooks by the neck of his jersey and the two began shoving each other in the face, shoulders and neck as their teammates tried to break up the scuffle. The Warriors’ broadcasters said it was Yusef Wright, a member of Golden State’s security and longtime bodyguard for Steph Curry , who was able to pull Green away from his opponent. “You don’t want that to escalate at all,” the announcer said after. Draymond Green was assessed a double technical on this play and was ejected. pic.twitter.com/uCmsTQxmcX — NBA on ESPN (@ESPNNBA) November 3, 2026 Brooks received a technical foul for his part in the scuffle, while Green was handed two technical fouls, resulting in an immediate ejection. Monday’s ejection was Green’s 31st since his NBA career began 15 years ago, per ESPN . Speaking to reporters after the game, a 116-113 victory for Golden State, Brooks claimed he was “just trying to de-escalate” the situation between Green and Maluach after the hard foul, according to ESPN . “He was just tweaking all game,” Brooks claimed of Green, who did not speak with the media on Monday. Draymond Green on Nov. 2, 2026 in San Francisco, CA Credit: Noah Graham/NBAE via Getty Meanwhile, Warriors head coach Steve Kerr chalked up the fiery moment to healthy competition between athletes. “That’s just the greatest NBA basketball players on earth competing,” Kerr said , noting, “Nothing serious happened.” Follow your favorite athletes on and off the field with PEOPLE’s free sports newsletter — sign up now! Curry said Green “lit a fire in all of us” and told reporters he was “glad” he and his teammates were able to pull off the win. “We had to respond,” said Curry. Next, the Warriors will host the Miami Heat on Thursday, Nov. 5. Read the original article on People

item.title: Spanish police open possible involuntary manslaughter investigation after tragic death of Tenerife’s Jesús de Miguel
item.description: Spanish police open possible involuntary manslaughter investigation after tragic death of Tenerife’s Jesús de Miguel An official police investigation has been opened, following the tragic events in Monday’s meeting between Tenerife and FC Andorra in Spanish football’s 2nd tier. Yesterday’s Segunda clash was abandoned late on, after Tenerife star Jesús de Miguel was stretchered from the field of play amid alarming scenes. Taken out by a flying challenge from Andorra goalkeeper Jesús Owono, De Miguel was taken straight to a nearby hospital, where he was placed in intensive care after suffering a cardiac arrest. In tragic news for the 30-year-old’s family, friends and all at Tenerife, De Miguel’s death was confirmed on Tuesday. Owing to the nature of the incident which culminated in his passing, an official investigation has since been opened by not only the Spanish football authorities, but also the National Police. As per a report from ESPN : ‘Spanish police have opened an investigation into possible involuntary manslaughter after Tenerife forward Jesús de Miguel died following an on-field collision.’ It is added that ‘under Spanish law, deaths from non-natural causes, including accidents, are subject to judicial investigation.’ We at Get Football send our condolences to all affected by Jesús de Miguel’s untimely passing. Conor Laird – GSFN

item.title: The Hornets Look Lost Without LaMelo Ball
item.description: Nov 2, 2026; Minneapolis, Minnesota, USA; Minnesota Timberwolves guard LaMelo Ball (1) smiles as he answers questions following the win over the Milwaukee Bucks at Target Center. | Source: Lastwordonsports.com - Jimmy Vik The Charlotte Hornets just got their doors blown off again, falling 124-91 to the Detroit Pistons and dropping to 3-5. The painful truth is staring them in the face: this offense doesn’t know how to function without LaMelo Ball . The former franchise point guard, now a Minnesota Timberwolf after Charlotte traded Ball for Naz Reid and draft capital, was the engine that made everything go. Without him, the Hornets don’t have an identity. It’s becoming evident that trading Ball wasn’t a move made in the interest of winning basketball games — at least not right now. Charlotte’s Offense May Be the Worst in the League Nov 2, 2026; Charlotte, North Carolina, USA; Detroit Pistons guard Kevin Huerter (27) defends against Charlotte Hornets guard Dennis Schroder (17) during the second half at Spectrum Center. Mandatory Credit: Jim Dedmon-Imagn Images Coming into the new season, the offense was expected to still be good — even without Ball. After all, Brandon Miller , Coby White , and Kon Knueppel are still on the team. However, that has not been the case. In eight games, the Hornets have failed to reach the 25-point mark in a quarter 18 times, meaning they’re coming up short in 56.25 percent of all quarters played. This has led to the Hornets owning the worst offensive rating in the league (100.5). A major contributing factor is that the high volume of three-pointers launched isn’t converting to points. The only player shooting above a 35 percent clip from beyond the arc is Grayson Allen . His consistent three-point shooting (currently 46.6% at 7.3 attempts per game) is what makes Allen a Sixth Man of the Year candidate . As a whole, the Hornets are shooting 29.6 percent from three-point range, ranking second-to-last in the league. If Charlotte were shooting closer to their uber-efficient 37.8 percent from last season, the narrative would be completely different. Historic Offense When LaMelo Ball Led the Way The Hornets became one of the teams to watch last season during their midseason turnaround. Led by Ball, they looked virtually unstoppable in a lot of games. As a matter of fact, the Hornets had the largest average margin of victory (in wins) at +18.1 points last season. Not only was this the biggest margin in the league, but it was the largest in league history. Ball’s gravity as a lethal shooter and playmaker gave his teammates plenty of great looks. With that creativity gone, those created advantages have been erased. Ball had things that he needed to improve on, but the talent was undeniable. Hornets offense last 15 games: 1st (121.6) Hornets defense last 15 games: 5th (110.4) Hornets net rating last 15 games: 1st (+11.2) https://t.co/Zj4aVT2pyr pic.twitter.com/MpCsBGOp5P — Basketball University (@UofBasketball) January 27, 2026 Kn

General Manager Jeff Peterson betting against Ball hinged on reasons like whether he was actually injury-prone or couldn’t embrace physicality. The Last Word Peterson asked Hornets fans for patience . So far, though, his plan to trade Ball is going sideways, and that patience runs thin when you’ve already been decimated on your home court twice this season. The Hornets’ offense is in shambles, and there’s an argument to be made that Knueppel could elevate it from being the worst offense in the league. But it’s hard to imagine this offense being anywhere close to how great it was last season with Ball. One of the biggest gambles that this organization has taken looks to have already backfired. Watching Ball have success in Minnesota while Charlotte struggles to do anything on offense is exactly what fans feared would happen when you remove one of the most impactful offensive creators in the NBA. Maybe Hornets basketball will look different when everyone is healthy, but the more likely scenario from the eight-game sample is that this offense won’t reach the heights of last season. item.title: Seahawks hit with harsh reality check after getting ‘smacked physically’ by Bears
item.description: Matt Kartozian-Imagn Images Seahawks hit with harsh reality check after getting ‘smacked physically’ by Bears appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Seattle Seahawks were humbled on Monday night, after losing 34-17 to the Chicago Bears. The usually reliable Seahawks defense got exposed, especially in the red zone. Seattle is now getting issued a stern warning by an NFL insider. “The worst red zone defense in the NFL…..no answers tonight. The Bears out hit them, the Bears out played them,” analyst Brock Huard said, per Seattle Sports. The #Seahawks got "smacked physically in a way we have not in years," says @BrockHuard in his reaction to the 34-17 loss, presented by @Puyallup_Tribe . Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) More reaction & analysis at https://t.co/sy672x5HGZ . pic.twitter.com/AhXHoDB6oX — Seattle Sports (@SeattleSports) November 3, 2026 It was certainly a tough night for Seattle. Offensively, the team couldn’t run the football. Defensively, Seattle got absolutely torched in the red zone. Huard went on to describe the game, and held absolutely nothing back. “We got smacked physically in a way we have not in years,” Huard added. His words ring true. Seattle’s defense allowed 363 total yards to the Bears. Seattle also went just 1-for-11 on third down, in a rough performance . “We got beat. No other way to sugar coat it,” Seahawks head coach Mike Macdonald said, per the Associated Press. “When you look at the things that it takes to win in our league, we didn’t do those things and they did.” Seattle seemed especially bothered by Bears defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons . Simmons seemed to bother Seahawks quarterback Sam Darnold all night. “According to Next Gen Stats, the Seahawks were held to 3.0 yards per play (3 sacks, INT) in the 48 plays where Simmons was on the field. In the eight plays where he was off the field, Seattle averaged 13.3 yards per play,” ESPN reported. Seattle is looking to win another Super Bowl this season. This type of performance certainly won’t help them in the weeks moving forward. The Seahawks will now try to regroup. The team next plays the Arizona Cardinals on Sunday. Seattle is now 4-4 on the year. Related: What Seahawks’ Sam Darnold said after stinking it up against Jeffery Simmons-led Bears pressure Related: Ref pool report explains 3 controversial plays that went against Seahawks vs. Bears

item.title: Mizzou’s 9-3 Record Could Still Land A Playoff Spot
item.description: Denny Medley-Imagn Images A 9-3 record usually means a team goes home early, but the Missouri Tigers might be the exception this year. The 19th-ranked Tigers defeated Arkansas 34-10 on Halloween night in Fayetteville to improve their season to 6-2. While a three-loss finish often disqualifies a team from the College Football Playoff, a new survey from SBN Reacts asks fans if Mizzou can still make the cut with that exact record. The answer depends on how they handle a brutal final stretch of games. A Gauntlet of Ranked Teams Per Rock M Nation , Missouri faces the second toughest remaining schedule in the entire country according to reports. The Tigers must host No. 10 Texas, travel to No. 2 Georgia, play at home against No. 8 Kentucky, and finish against Oklahoma. These four games alone decide if the season ends in a bowl game or a playoff berth. There is almost no room for error after losing to Mississippi State and Ole Miss earlier in the year. Penalties Cost Big Gains Even when the team plays well, self-inflicted wounds often hurt the final result. Caleb Goodie Sr. nullified a 16-yard gain by Jamal Roberts via a holding penalty during the recent victory against Arkansas. Offense momentum stalled as the squad finished with nine penalties totaling 80 yards. Head coach Eliah Drinkwitz admitted the struggle in his postgame comments. “Offensively, we were just continually stubbing our toes with penalties,” Drinkwitz said. “We’ve got to get that cleaned up. In the second half, we were much better.” Despite the penalty issues, the offense found new ways to move the ball. Quarterback Austin Simmons and wide receiver DeMarion Fowlkes used jet sweeps and designed runs to keep the defense guessing. Muscling through for a six-yard gain on a jet sweep, the 5-foot-9 receiver Fowlkes executed just one cut before the play concluded. This unique play call helped the Tigers secure a 13-0 lead before halftime and eventually win the game. The coaching staff used these east-west plays to generate quick touches for their best players. Running Backs Lead the Charge Jamal Roberts carried the ball 23 times for 138 yards and one touchdown against Arkansas. This performance pushed his season total past 1,000 rushing yards, making him the 53rd player in program history to reach that mark. He currently leads the entire Power Four conference with 1,005 rushing yards through eight games. The defense also stepped up when it mattered most on Saturday night. Junior linebacker Nicholas Rodriguez made nine total tackles and forced a fumble to help secure the victory. Safety Trajen Greco added eight tackles, an interception, and a pass deflection to stop Arkansas drives. Greco now has three interceptions on the year, which ties for second in the SEC. These individual efforts show why Mizzou has won five straight games in the Battle Line Rivalry. The question remains whether the team can survive the final four games to reach nine wins. item.title: Can Iowa Keep Momentum at Northwestern?
item.description: IOWA CITY, IOWA- OCTOBER 26: Running back Kamari Moulton #28 of the Iowa Hawkeyes runs through a hole during the first half against the Northwestern Wildcats at Kinnick Stadium on October 26, 2024 in Iowa City, Iowa. (Photo by Matthew Holst/Getty Images) | Getty Images Well, that’s more like it. One week after handing away the pig in Minneapolis, the Hawkeyes took out every ounce of frustration on #25 Wisconsin in a 30-0 shutout that kept the Heartland Trophy in Iowa City for a fifth straight year. The dominant performance also put Iowa back in the AP poll at #21 and the Coaches Poll at #20. Hank Brown was surgical in his return to the lineup (20-of-24 for 222 yards and two scores. The performance was good enough to win Big Ten Offensive Player of the Week (when is the last time Iowa had their QB win that award?). He spread the ball around to 7 different receivers with DJ Vonnahme, Reece Vander Zee and Tony Diaz all topping 50 yards on the day. The defense allowed just 52 rushing yards and nine first downs and the one-week character check came back emphatic. The reward is a genuinely fascinating road trip. The roughly $870 million, 35,000-seat palace on the lakefront opened a month ago and bills itself as the most expensive college football stadium ever built. Despite the smaller size, it’s still a haven for visiting fans. Tickets for this weekend’s matchup are largely in line with the cost to buy season tickets to the Wildcats. item.content:encoded: IOWA CITY, IOWA- OCTOBER 26: Running back Kamari Moulton #28 of the Iowa Hawkeyes runs through a hole during the first half against the Northwestern Wildcats at Kinnick Stadium on October 26, 2024 in Iowa City, Iowa. (Photo by Matthew Holst/Getty Images) | Getty Images Well, that’s more like it. One week after handing away the pig in Minneapolis, the Hawkeyes took out every ounce of frustration on #25 Wisconsin in a 30-0 shutout that kept the Heartland Trophy in Iowa City for a fifth straight year. The dominant performance also put Iowa back in the AP poll at #21 and the Coaches Poll at #20. Hank Brown was surgical in his return to the lineup (20-of-24 for 222 yards and two scores. The performance was good enough to win Big Ten Offensive Player of the Week (when is the last time Iowa had their QB win that award?). He spread the ball around to 7 different receivers with DJ Vonnahme, Reece Vander Zee and Tony Diaz all topping 50 yards on the day. The defense allowed just 52 rushing yards and nine first downs and the one-week character check came back emphatic. The reward is a genuinely fascinating road trip. Iowa heads to Evanston to take on Northwestern on Saturday night (6:30 pm CT on FOX) for its first look at the new Ryan Field. The roughly $870 million, 35,000-seat palace on the lakefront opened a month ago and bills itself as the most expensive college football stadium ever built. Despite the smaller size, it’s still a haven for visiting fans. Tickets for this weekend’s matchup are largely in line with the cost to buy season tickets to the Wildcats. Both teams enter the week at 6-2 overall and 3-2 in Big Ten play. Both have been ranked in recent weeks, but it’s Iowa now moving up after the big win over the Badgers while Northwestern finds themselves just outside the top-25 this week after falling on the road ta Oregon last Saturday. Despite the loss, FanDuel Sportsbook has Northwestern favored by 1.5 in this one with an over/under of 44.5 total points. So Iowa is a road dog to a team it has beaten four straight times, with an implied final somewhere around 23-21. The books are telling you this Northwestern team is different. And they may have a case. A Different Northwestern The David Braun rebuild is fully realized now. Four years after taking over as the interim HC, he’s won two bowls, banked a Big Ten Coach of the Year award, signed an extension through 2031 and built a 6-2 team whose only losses are one-score road games at Indiana and Oregon. There are no bad losses on the resume. There’s also a distinctly Iowa-flavored footnote: Braun cut his teeth on Northern Iowa’s staff before his NDSU years, so he knows exactly what kind of football is coming Saturday. The biggest change this year is on offense, where Northwestern handed the play sheet to Chip Kelly. He inherited Michigan State transfer Aidan Chiles and has turned him into one of the most efficient quarterbacks in the conference. Chiles is completing 68.8% of his passes for 1,898 yards with 13 touchdowns and only single interception, plus 10 more scores on the ground. Caleb Komolafe (618 yards) and Joseph Himon II (8.9 a carry) power a rushing attack ranked 24th nationally, and SDSU transfer Griffin Wilde (44-761-5) is a legitimate WR1. They convert 46.5% of their third downs. This is not the 12-points-a-game Northwestern of recent memory – it’s a top top-35 scoring offense (33.6 PPG) and a top-30 total offense (438.1 yards per game). The flip side is a defense that will statistically be the worst Iowa has faced since the opener. The Wildcats rank 84th in total defense, 75th against the run, 94th against the pass and tied for 100th in sacks with 13 all season. Northwestern seems to have taken a page out of the Phil Parker book and is seemingly happy to give up yardage as long as they can hold opponents to FGs. While the Wildcats rank poorly on yards allowed, they remain top-25 in scoring defense, giving up 18.75 points per game thanks to the 16th best red zone defense (tied with Iowa). Northwestern is holding opponents to a FG or scoreless on 57% of their red zone trips. The Matchup Stat to Watch Turnover margin: Northwestern is +10, fifth in the country. Iowa is +1. Everything about Iowa’s season (and frankly, the KF tenure) says that column decides the outcome Saturday. The Minneapolis loss featured four giveaways all by itself while the wins have been built on clean football and a defense that ranks 4th nationally in both points allowed (12.5) and rushing yards allowed (79.0). Chiles has thrown just one interception in eight games and Phil Parker’s unit has to be the one that finally makes him flinch. The pass rush is tied for 11th nationally with 24 sacks and is facing an offense that has barely turned it over all year, making this the chess match of the night. On the other side, Iowa’s offense gets the most forgiving matchup it has seen since the trip to Seattle. An offensive line that has spent the season among the nation’s stingiest in sacks allowed faces a front with 13 all year. Xavier Williams and L.J. Phillips face the 75th-ranked run defense and the Hawkeyes will have to be able to run the ball. If Iowa’s 70th-ranked scoring offense can’t find the mid-20s against this group, it’s an answer about the offense, not the opponent. Last week, more than 60% of the community thought we already had that question answered against Minnesota. The Wisconsin performance likely shifts the view, but falling flat again this week against a mediocre Northwestern team would seem to indicate Wisconsin was the anomaly, not Minnesota. Here’s a quick look at the details for Saturday’s matchup. Date: Saturday, November 7 Time: 6:30 pm CT Matchup: #21 Iowa Hawkeyes (6-2, 3-2) at Northwestern Wildcats (6-2, 3-2) Location: Ryan Field, Evanston, Illinois TV: FOX Initial Weather Forecast: Mostly cloudy, game-time temps in the upper 40s with light wind off the lake FanDuel Opening Line : Northwestern -1.5 O/U 44.5 Series History Iowa leads this series by nearly 30 games all-time, thanks in large part to a 21-game winning streak from 1974 to 1994. The Hawkeyes are trying to start another long streak, having won the last four and six of the last ten. The Wildcats are no longer a doormat, though, so expecting this streak to last too terribly long is a fool’s dream. The two team’s didn’t face off last year and last saw each other in 2024 when the Hawkeyes won 40-14. The 2023 meeting came in Wrigley Field (Iowa won 10-7), so the Hawkeyes haven’t played in Evanston since the current streak started back in 2021 when Iowa won 17-12. Northwestern hasn’t beaten Iowa at home since 2017 and head coach Ryan Braun is 0-2 against Kirk Ferentz. No trophy changes hands in this one, but the calendar supplies some unique history. Saturday is November 7, marking 17 years to the day since unranked Northwestern walked into Kinnick and stunned a 9-0 Iowa team that sat #4 in the BCS standings, 17-10, after Ricky Stanzi went down with an ankle injury Different era of Northwestern football, same lesson: this program has enjoys ruining great Iowa seasons.

item.title: Politano: ‘Napoli are fragile at the moment, but no alibi against Porto’
item.description: Politano: ‘Napoli are fragile at the moment, but no alibi against Porto’ Matteo Politano admits Napoli are ‘fragile’ defensively and concede too easily, but mustn’t ‘use injuries as an alibi’ for the Champions League trip to FC Porto. It kicks off at the Estadio do Dragao on Wednesday at 20.00 GMT (21.00 CET). The Partenopei are playing catch-up in the tournament after one win and two defeats, but that is still better than their opponents, who lost all three matches so far in the Champions League. Max Allegri’s side also stumbled in Serie A at the weekend, losing 2-0 away to Juventus. Politano sees Napoli problems NAPLES, ITALY – OCTOBER 20: Matteo Politano of SSC Napoli celebrates scoring his team’s first goal during the UEFA Champions League 2026/27 League Phase MD3 match between SSC Napoli and FK Bodo/Glimt at Stadio Diego Armando Maradona on October 20, 2026 in Naples, Italy. (Photo by Francesco Pecoraro/Getty Images) “A difficult game awaits us tomorrow. It’s true that we have some injuries, but this mustn’t be used as an alibi, we don’t want alibis at this moment,” said Politano in his press conference. “We are the only ones who can drag ourselves out of this situation. We’ve got to give our all on the pitch, because this is a fundamental match for us.” NAPLES, ITALY – APRIL 06: Matteo Politano of SSC Napoli celebrates after scoring the opening goal during the Serie A match between SSC Napoli and AC Milan at Stadio Diego Armando Maradona on April 06, 2026 in Naples, Italy. (Photo by Francesco Pecoraro/Getty Images) The recurring problem for Napoli this season is how many goals they are conceding, and assistant manager Marco Landucci confirmed players backing off when defending is not something suggested by the coaching staff. “When we concede goals, it’s everyone’s fault and not just the defenders, this is a team sport,” confessed Politano. “We are fragile at the moment, we can’t seem to defend as well as we did in previous years. We lack determination in pressing the opponents, so naturally against quality players you are going to pay for that. “We’ve got to come together as a unit and try from tomorrow to be more solid. We haven’t tested the line-up yet, so we don’t know if it’ll be three or four at the back, but it is no problem for me.” ITALY – OCTOBER 28: Matteo Politano of SSC Napoli celebrates after scoring team’s second goal during the Serie A match between AC Monza and SSC Napoli at U-Power Stadium on October 28, 2026 in Italy. (Photo by Pier Marco Tacca/Getty Images) Napoli fumbled a lead for the 3-1 Champions League defeat to Villarreal , and Politano made a very costly error with a howler of a back-pass. “Unfortunately, we can do nothing about the past, we need to focus on the future,” added the winger. “I challenge myself every single day to give more, I’ve won a lot with this team, but I’ve got to keep pushing. It’s not an easy situation, we’ve all got to come together and stay concentrated at all times. “Porto are a strong si

item.title: Rumor Opens Door For NY Giants & Philadelphia Eagles Blockbuster Trade, But It’s Not For Saquon Barkley
item.description: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect A new NFL trade rumor opens the door for the New York Giants to address a major need in a deal with rivals, the Philadelphia Eagles , before next week’s deadline. The Giants and Eagles head into the Week 9 NFL schedule in very different positions. New York has been one of the feel-good stories in the NFL this season, because despite losing their starting quarterback and top pass rusher, they sit atop the NFC East with a 4-2-1 record. On the flip side, injuries — especially to Jalen Hurts — have had a far bigger effect on Philadelphia’s 2-6 record over the first half of the season. Ahead of the Nov. 10 trade deadline, reports point to the Giants being buyers, while the Eagles could be big sellers. But could the two NFC East teams actually work together on a deal? With New York allegedly looking to upgrade the running back spot, a trade for Saquon Barkley seems intriguing. It would give them the elite back they want, while righting the wrong of letting him leave Big Blue for Philly in free agency two years ago. However, recent reports claim the Eagles have informed the three-time Pro Bowler that they have no plans to move him. NFL insider Jason LaCanfora backed up that belief in a Tuesday report when he suggested Barkley is near untouchable. But there is a different star who would address a Giants need and might be up for grabs before the deadline. Should the New York Giants pursue a Jalen Carter trade? Oct 11, 2026; Tottenham, ENG; Philadelphia Eagles defensive tackle Jalen Carter (98) reacts during the second half against the Jacksonville Jaguars at Tottenham Hotspur Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Kirby Lee-Imagn Images “Executives have also long wondered whether the Eagles would be able to retain both former first-round defensive tackle selections, Jordan Davis and Jalen Carter . But Philadelphia won’t sell low on either if a deal presents itself,” LaCanfora wrote. The word around the NFL is that the Giants are trying to find upgrades at running back and the interior of their defensive line after trading Dexter Lawrence in the offseason. The two-time Pro Bowler would absolutely fill that void. Furthermore, the 25-year-old is also under contract for five more seasons . The big question is what would the price be? The Giants got the 10th overall pick in April’s draft for Lawrence, who is a three-time Pro Bowler and only three years older than Carter. It is possible the Eagles ask for a first-rounder plus a future Day 3 pick for the talented defensive tackle. Do you think the G-Men would be willing to pay that price? item.content:encoded: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect A new NFL trade rumor opens the door for the New York Giants to address a major need in a deal with rivals, the Philadelphia Eagles , before next week’s deadline. The Giants and Eagles head into the Week 9 NFL schedule in very different positions. New York has been one of the feel-good stories in the NFL this season, because despite losing their starting quarterback and top pass rusher, they sit atop the NFC East with a 4-2-1 record. On the flip side, injuries — especially to Jalen Hurts — have had a far bigger effect on Philadelphia’s 2-6 record over the first half of the season. Ahead of the Nov. 10 trade deadline, reports point to the Giants being buyers, while the Eagles could be big sellers. But could the two NFC East teams actually work together on a deal? With New York allegedly looking to upgrade the running back spot, a trade for Saquon Barkley seems intriguing. It would give them the elite back they want, while righting the wrong of letting him leave Big Blue for Philly in free agency two years ago. However, recent reports claim the Eagles have informed the three-time Pro Bowler that they have no plans to move him. NFL insider Jason LaCanfora backed up that belief in a Tuesday report when he suggested Barkley is near untouchable. But there is a different star who would address a Giants need and might be up for grabs before the deadline. Should the New York Giants pursue a Jalen Carter trade? Oct 11, 2026; Tottenham, ENG; Philadelphia Eagles defensive tackle Jalen Carter (98) reacts during the second half against the Jacksonville Jaguars at Tottenham Hotspur Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Kirby Lee-Imagn Images “Executives have also long wondered whether the Eagles would be able to retain both former first-round defensive tackle selections, Jordan Davis and Jalen Carter . But Philadelphia won’t sell low on either if a deal presents itself,” LaCanfora wrote. The word around the NFL is that the Giants are trying to find upgrades at running back and the interior of their defensive line after trading Dexter Lawrence in the offseason. The two-time Pro Bowler would absolutely fill that void. Furthermore, the 25-year-old is also under contract for five more seasons . The big question is what would the price be? The Giants got the 10th overall pick in April’s draft for Lawrence, who is a three-time Pro Bowler and only three years older than Carter. It is possible the Eagles ask for a first-rounder plus a future Day 3 pick for the talented defensive tackle. Do you think the G-Men would be willing to pay that price? item.title: Blue Jays Cut Ties With Gold Glover After Just Two Seasons
item.description: Toronto Blue Jays outfielder Myles Straw One year after winning the American League and coming two outs away from winning the World Series, the Toronto Blue Jays missed the postseason entirely this year. Some stars underperforming and injuries held the Blue Jays back, despite the team taking an aggressive approach in free agency. This offseason is a very important one for the Blue Jays as they look to get back into October in a stacked American League East. The team has already started making some roster moves as free agency begins, and one of the moves they made was declining Myles Straw's $8 million club option, making him a free agent. Straw won a Gold Glove Award with the Cleveland Guardians in 2022 as a center fielder. The Blue Jays acquired him in a trade in 2025. In the last two seasons, he has played all three outfield spots, but has spent most of his time in left field and center field. Looking for the perfect gift for a baseball player in your life? Check out our brand new baseball lifestyle brand! Offensively, he posted a .662 OPS in the last two seasons. Even though his OPS was not great, he posted a .262 batting average in 2025, proving he could at least be a consistent force getting on base. This year, his batting average and on-base percentage both dropped. Simply put, he did not play like a player worth $8 million. The Blue Jays gave him a $1.75 million buyout, and adding a quality outfielder will be a huge focus for the team. There are already reports that they are interested in Seiya Suzuki. He would be a huge upgrade for their outfield. More MLB: Mets Reportedly Cooling On Japanese Slugger Teruaki Sato For This Reason

item.title: ‘I threw that cup in the trash’: Fan reacts after LeBron James sips his wine
item.description: Oct 20, 2026; New York, New York, USA; Philadelphia 76ers forward LeBron James (23) on the court before the start of the second quarter against the New York Knicks at Madison Square Garden. Mandatory Credit: Brad Penner-Imagn Images LeBron James has never hidden his love of wine. On Monday night, he got an unexpected taste in the middle of a game. While chasing a loose ball during the Philadelphia 76ers’ win over the Chicago Bulls, James crashed into a fan holding a cup of red wine. So he grabbed the cup and took a sip before heading back onto the court. LeBron Drinks Fan’s Wine James has been off to a strong start in his first season in Philadelphia. The 76ers improved to 7-1 with a 126-107 win over the Bulls on Monday, and James finished with 15 points, seven rebounds, and nine assists. However, it was an incident that happened in the stands that stole the headlines. During the third quarter, with the 76ers up by 11. James collided with the fan while chasing the ball out of bounds, then took a sip from his cup, as seen in video of the moment . After the game, James explained what happened. “I spilled some of his wine. I crashed into him, spilled some of his wine. So I wanted to see if it was worth it on my arm and how good it was. It was all right,” James said, via ESPN’s Kris Rhim . ‘I Threw That Cup in the Trash’ The fan, longtime Sixers season-ticket holder Troy Clemons, wasn’t upset about it, either. “I’m just glad for him to be here,” Clemons told ESPN . “I’m not worried about the wine getting on me.” Rhim also asked Clemons what he did with the cup James drank from. Clemons didn’t keep it as a souvenir. “At the end of the day, he’s another man like me. I mean, he’s LeBron. But at the end of the day, I threw that cup in the trash,” Clemons said. He added that he didn’t mean any disrespect by it. “It’s nothing up with him. I just got a fresh drink, though,” Clemons said. Needless to say, it’s a moment he won’t forget anytime soon, even if he didn’t save the cup. The post ‘I threw that cup in the trash’: Fan reacts after LeBron James sips his wine appeared first on The Comeback: Today’s Top Sports Stories & Reactions .

item.title: Jon Rahm Rejects LIV 2.0, Eyes PGA Tour Return
item.description: Jerod Ringwald-Imagn Images The two-time Major winner turned down an offer to stay with the LIV Golf League under its new 2.0 structure. He told reporters that the revised plan simply did not feel right for his career path. This decision comes as the tour navigates a shift in leadership and financial backing. Rahm is now looking toward a potential return to the PGA Tour while serving a suspension. The Spanish star made these comments during his pre‑tournament press conference. The tournament will be his first official start on the DP World Tour since leaving the Saudi-backed circuit. He reflected on his time away, noting that while he enjoyed the experience, the future direction of the league was not inspiring. He told reporters, “Well, I would say I can only reflect on those three years as a positive. It was a wonderful experience. Played a lot of good golf. Obviously individually and as a team, we did great.” Despite the success he found in the team format, the changes proposed for LIV 2.0 were a dealbreaker. As reported by Yahoo News Singapore , Rahm explained that he “wasn’t thrilled with the changes they were doing to 2.0 and I just wasn’t willing to follow that path.” He felt the league was moving away from what made it unique and becoming too much like a regular tour. The exit of the Saudi PIF as backers has left the league in flux, with new creditors BC Partners attempting to launch a second iteration in 2027. Rahm noted there were “too many unknowns at the time” regarding the commitment deadline. He felt the proposal lacked the special qualities that defined the original concept. His focus has now shifted to the PGA Tour, though a formal return has not been finalized. Rahm revealed he has not yet had a conversation with the tour about his reinstatement. He told the press, “As of right now, I really don’t know what 2027 is going to look like for me.” Earlier in the year, the PGA Tour offered a deal similar to the one Brooks Koepka accepted, which involved a $5 million donation to charity and restrictions on sponsor exemptions. Rahm, along with Bryson DeChambeau and Cameron Smith, did not agree to those terms by the deadline. The tour has since gone silent on the matter, leaving the timing of his return uncertain. The Path Forward for the Spaniard Rahm’s rejection of the LIV 2.0 offer signals a preference for the traditional tour model. He valued the team aspect of LIV 1.0 but could not accept the diluted vision of the new version. His comments suggest a player who prioritizes the competitive integrity of the game over the potential for a massive, albeit uncertain, payout from a restructured league. The financial incentives of the PGA Tour Champions or a new LIV deal did not sway him when the core product changed. He continues to compete on the DP World Tour while awaiting a decision on his PGA Tour reinstatement. Rahm chose to wait rather than accept a compromised deal. He is willing to play on the DP World Tour while the PGA Tour decides

item.title: DeForest Buckner gets his old number back
item.description: Photo by Michael Owens/Getty Images) | Getty Images Not that it was ever a mystery, DeForest Buckner’s return to the San Francisco 49ers means he’s getting his old No. 99 back. That number has been worn by second-year defensive tackle CJ West. Buckner said he got to know West last week and the two were talking, where West told Buckner, “Hey, bro, 99 is yours.” West will wear No. 90. Buckner didn’t need to ask for the number. He said West offered it to him. Buckner vowed to “take care” of West, even though CJ asked for nothing in return. Buckner denied telling the Colts he only wanted to be traded to the 49ers. He also wouldn’t say whether he’s discussed or focused on a potential extension with the 49ers after this season. His focus is on the remainder of the season. “Fred and I were just talking in the cafe this morning. You really wanna be a team on the rise. This is a part of the season where, you know, some teams start falling off. The really select group continues to rise and get better every week. That’s what I’m doing. That’s what I’m trying to do.” During Buckner’s press conference on Monday, he said some of his new teammates told him Kris Kocurek plays a lot of 2019 film as teaching tape. The nostalgia is great, but the 49ers brought in Buckner to do a job and do it at a high level. He said he plans to do everything he can to help elevate the defensive line room. When asked about the immediate impact he could make, Buckner leaned into his experience, but also wants to help the young players in the room: “There’s a lot of young guys in the room. I’m an open book. If they want to pick my brain and ask me questions, I’m always an open book to all of them. It doesn’t take just one or two guys to make a room or make a team. It’s the entire room. I’ve always believed that the d-line is the engine of the team. And I wanna pour into those young guys everything that I know, so I can help their game and get even better.” How the snaps look with Buckner in the fold is one of the more intriguing parts about the defense moving forward. Buckner still has the stamina to play 70-75% of the time. That means whoever is next to him will be rotated quite a bit to keep them fresh.

item.title: Tenerife footballer Jesús de Miguel dies aged 30 after on-pitch collision
item.description: Police homicide division opens judicial proceedings He was struck in the chest when challenging for ball Spanish football was in shock on Tuesday after the Tenerife striker Jesús de Miguel died after a collision with the Andorra goalkeeper Jesús Owono during a match in the second division. The homicide division of the national police has opened judicial proceedings into a possible involuntary manslaughter, a routine procedure after any death not by natural causes. The chief public prosecutor in Santa Cruz de Tenerife told the state news agency EFE that it was “very difficult” for a case to come to court. Tenerife announced that De Miguel had died at 8am on Tuesday after he had been taken into intensive care on Monday afternoon. He did not regain consciousness after a cardiorespiratory arrest. Continue reading...

item.title: Football Daily | West Ham want promotion – so it’s time to call in an understated club legend
item.description: Sign up now! Sign up now! Sign up now? Sign up now! While Football Daily hasn’t actually seen much of West Ham this season, we’ve noted enough of their results to presume they were doing OK in their attempt to bounce back to the Premier League after relegation. Less than a third of the way through the Championship season under Nuno Espírito Santo, they’d already spanked six without reply past both Wrexham and Lincoln, while scoring three or more in wins over Wolves, Derby and Bolton. However, it turns out that of the 13 matches they’ve played in a league that is famously difficult to get out of (unless you were Sheffield Wednesday last season ), they have actually lost three times and currently sit in eighth place, a whopping six points off leaders Middlesbrough. Given the context of such an unbridgeable chasm, it is small wonder West Ham fans woke up to news that Nuno had been unceremoniously bounced out of the London Stadium with a P45 in hand. While my heart aches for Jesús de Miguel, who has died after a collision with the Andorra goalkeeper Jesús Owono, I shudder to think the trauma that shall haunt Owono for the rest of his life. I do hope and pray the wider community understands and extends their support in his recuperation” – Krishna Moorthy. As an upgrade to Steve Plever’s suggestion of paper thin shirts [ Monday’s letters ]: how about Velcro shirts? If the bit comes off, it is a shirt pull and the offender has the honour of putting it back in place before being awarded a yellow card” – Mike Harold. To dive or not to dive seems to be biggest dilemma in the Premier League right now. It’s not. The problem with today’s highly paid professionals is that they simply have no panache at all when they go down. I recall watching Francis Lee pick up the ball on the halfway line at a mud soaked Maine Road in the late 1960s, he put his head down and headed for goal, he was determined, he was single minded. He was 30 yards from goal, he was in full flow. He was tackled from behind and then he really took off, he grew wings, he soared. I swear he landed in the penalty area over 10 yards away. He dragged himself to his feet and without a semblance of a smile smashed the well-deserved penalty, with a very heavy leather ball straight at the centre of the goal at over 70 mph. The goalkeeper, obviously no fool, simply dived out of the way. The press christened him “Lee Won Pen” He was my hero. That man had panache, he had style” – Myles Flynn. I am interested to read that Aston Villa considered the words of Jamie Carragher “unacceptable insults” . It would obviously help matters if they could publish examples of acceptable insults” – Rupert Jeffery. This is an extract from our daily football email … Football Daily. To get the full version, just visit this page and follow the instructions . Continue reading...

item.title: ‘An absolute afterthought’: the story of the Nigeria women’s team’s fall from grace
item.description: The Super Falcons won’t be at the World Cup and with the prize money going up, they risk being left even further behind It was a historic result in Casablanca – but not in a good way. Nigeria’s 2-1 defeat against South Africa in a playoff in August meant that the Super Falcons are missing out on the World Cup for the first time. It is a crushing blow for the most decorated national side in Africa across both men and women, one that has won no fewer than 10 Wafcon titles . The journalist and lecturer Dr Victor Ademola was in Morocco the day of the defeat. “It was a very difficult evening,” he says. “Some players were visibly emotional while others appeared to be processing what had just happened. I saw players crying as they got on to the team bus while some sat alone or remained on their phones, looking very sad.” Continue reading...

item.title: Fifa to share documents on World Cup sell-off plans with council members
item.description: Viewings to take place at Fifa’s headquarters in Zurich No direct response to Uefa’s questions on governance Fifa will grant its council members access to documents regarding the doomed Fifa Forward Enterprise scheme but has not responded directly to more than 50 questions from Uefa about its governance and recent scandals. In a letter sent to the Fifa Council by Mattias Grafström, the governing body’s secretary general, members were told material relating to FFE will be released for them to view in person at Fifa’s headquarters in Zurich. They will be allowed only to view the documents, of which the exact nature and scope are unclear, under strict confidentiality protocols. A deadline of 16 November has been set to apply for such visits; eyebrows may be raised in some quarters about the fact this is two days before candidates for the Fifa election next year are required to declare their hand. Continue reading...

item.title: Revisiting the Superclásico: a story of death, violence, colour and family
item.description: Attending Boca v River in the week I turned 60 made me recall a lifetime of experiences at the fixture Ever since the Observer Sport Monthly published a list of 50 sporting things you must do before you die with Watch Boca Juniors Play River Plate in Buenos Aires at No 1 in 2004, the biggest super derby in Argentina has been firmly positioned in the global imagination; its reputation for colour, passion and uncontainable emotion acquiring an almost glamorous sheen. The thump and thud of the coordinated chants, the shiny ticker-tape amid flare smoke matching the teams’ strips, the bounce of the concrete as tens of thousands jump in unison, mounted police surrounding the stadium, avalanche stoppers set alight, rockets aimed at players; blood and fire. Exciting, right? Continue reading...

item.title: Stumbling block: Wirtz's and Liverpool’s costly struggles against tight defences | Andrew Beasley
item.description: Credit to Arsenal for restricting opportunities at Anfield but Iraola will need his side to learn to unpick low backlines Liverpool did not have a shot on target in their 1-0 defeat by Arsenal on Sunday, according to Opta, the first time they have drawn this type of blank in a Premier League game at Anfield since records began in 2003-04. They did not find the target in a goalless draw at the Emirates Stadium this year either, though in both games they struck the woodwork. The margins tend to be fine when recording statistical outliers. If Alexis Mac Allister’s floated ball from distance into David Raya’s waiting arms had actually counted as a shot, would Andoni Iraola’s side have delivered a markedly better attacking performance? Far more concerning for the Spaniard will be that his team had 52 touches in the Arsenal penalty area (which is good) to create only one Opta‑defined big chance (which is bad). The Premier League average this season is five times more efficient; 10.3 box touches per big chance. Continue reading...

item.title: Goals, guests and 6,561 scenarios: inside ESPN on the biggest NWSL Decision Day yet
item.description: The final day of the regular season gave fans Gotham’s Shield win, a farewell to a Seattle hero and a new part-whiparound, part-watchalong show to take it all in As a player, Ali Krieger went into NWSL Decision Day focused on one result. She was Gotham FC’s captain in 2023, the first time the league played all of the final games of the regular season simultaneously. The job, she remembers, was to not worry about the other games going on. Three years later, Krieger spent Decision Day with eyes on not one game but eight. For the first time, all of the final games of the NWSL season were aired by the same network. Krieger, now a lead analyst for ESPN, and host Kelsey Riggs Cuff anchored the coverage from headquarters in Bristol with a show that was part whiparound, part watchalong, and ultimately wholly new for the 14-year-old league. Continue reading...

item.title: Arsenal have everything they need to repeat as Premier League champions | Jonathan Wilson
item.description: Sunday’s win at Liverpool showed the Gunners are deeper, more experienced, and are playing against a weaker class of contenders than last season Sign up for our free newsletter here Arsenal are three points clear at the top of the Premier League table . But given the team in second are Manchester City, who are likely to be facing at the very least a major points deduction , perhaps more significant is that they are five clear of Brighton in third. The season of domination that many anticipated from the champions appears to be coming to pass. Liverpool challenged them on Sunday. There was a 20-minute spell before half-time when they swarmed all over Arsenal, and Anfield felt at least like it did in the golden years of Jürgen Klopp, when it buzzed with an energy that could overwhelm visitors. But Arsenal got through that, reset at half-time, and navigated the second half with relative comfort. For the second league game running, they denied Liverpool a shot on target. This is an extract from Soccer Desk, a newsletter from the Guardian US. Subscribe for free here . Continue reading...

item.title: Led by Liam Rosenior and backed by billionaires, Paris FC are now a force in Ligue 1 | Luke Entwistle
item.description: After a huge summer and with PSG’s other rivals falling away, their city rivals are aiming to ‘be one of the biggest clubs in Europe’ By Get French Football News It is hard to know what Pierre Ferracci found stranger: the fact that he was fully suited among a set of bare-chested Paris FC ultras singing his name or that, behind him, in what was the final game of his presidency, his team were playing Monaco off the park. “I didn’t see any of the first 15 minutes of the game because I was with the ultras,” he admitted. On the pitch, as well as in the stands, was evidence of how far his side has come since he joined back in 2006. At that time, Les Parisiens were in the amateur third tier of French football. Ferracci arrived initially in an administrative function before becoming owner and president in 2012. It was not until 2017 that his side reached Ligue 2. Continue reading...

item.title: Football Daily | Aston Villa, ‘unacceptable insults’ and thin-skinned clutching of pearls
item.description: Sign up now! Sign up now! Sign up now? Sign up now! When Jamie Carragher appeared as a pundit on Sky Sports Super Sunday, Football Daily was surprised he didn’t have a solicitor sitting alongside him, occasionally jotting notes on a pad or leaning over to give whispered instructions and answer “no comment” to any leading questions about Trey Nyoni starting ahead of Ryan Gravenberch. On Friday night, the former Liverpool defender was subjected to a threat of legal action from Aston Villa, who took such grave exception to some “unacceptable insults” he had rained down on them from his podcast pulpit, that they were ready to call in the heavy legal artillery and stop him from preventing their “ascension in English and European football”. Taking a leaf out of the tried-and-much-ridiculed Nottingham Forest playbook , Villa chair Nassef Sawiris appears to have eschewed contacting Carragher through the usual formal channels and instead cajoled some unfortunate junior comms staffer to make the portentous announcement on their Social Media Disgraces. Continue reading...

On Friday night, the former Liverpool defender was subjected to a threat of legal action from Aston Villa, who took such grave exception to some “unacceptable insults” he had rained down on them from his podcast pulpit, that they were ready to call in the heavy legal artillery and stop him from preventing their “ascension in English and European football”. Taking a leaf out of the tried-and-much-ridiculed Nottingham Forest playbook , Villa chair Nassef Sawiris appears to have eschewed contacting Carragher through the usual formal channels and instead cajoled some unfortunate junior comms staffer to make the portentous announcement on their Social Media Disgraces. Continue reading...

item.title: From VHS dreams to San Siro glory: Amorim’s Milan surge puts rivals on notice | Nicky Bandini
item.description: Inspired by the legendary Milan sides of his youth, the manager gave his side a lift with a tactical victory over Inter Ruben Amorim had waited a lifetime for his first Milan derby. As a kid growing up in Lisbon, he supported two football teams. There was the local one, Benfica, whose games he attended so early in life that his father has recalled changing nappies in the stands of the old Estádio da Luz. And the other one that captivated him from overseas. “I remember watching tapes of that Milan team with [Paolo] Maldini, [Franco] Baresi, [Ruud] Gullit, [Frank] Rijkaard, [Dejan] Savicevic,” Amorim told the Portuguese newspaper Expresso in 2017. “My childhood dreams were to play for Benfica and Milan. I’ve fulfilled one. Now I suppose I’ll have to become a coach for the other!” Continue reading...

item.title: Harry Kane’s Ballon d’Or party gives way to anxiety-filled hangover for Bayern Munich | Andy Brassell
item.description: Dortmund did not read the script, remaining level on points with the defending champions at the top of the table It was the moment they had all been … not so much waiting for, but planning, pushing and yearning for. In the videos that announce the starting lineup on the giant scoreboard before kick-off, every Bayern Munich player turns to face the camera with their personal salute, greeting or goal celebration, the playful progression from the standard folding of arms. Except on Saturday evening, the No 9 turned around smiling, and cradling the golden trophy. In the midweek DFB Pokal stroll against Magdeburg there had been a salute, the players welcoming Harry Kane on to the pitch with a guard of honour to commemorate his Ballon d’Or victory two nights before. This, however, was the real party, the moment where the England captain’s and Bayern’s successful union and the apex it has reached was celebrated in front of a global audience. There was every reason to believe it would be a full and satisfying victory lap, even in Der Klassiker, with proper competition so often bringing the best out of the Rekordmeister. Continue reading...

item.title: Nuno Espírito Santo under threat at West Ham after poor start to the season
item.description: Favourites for promotion sit eighth in Championship Key figures at club losing patience with manager Nuno Espírito Santo’s future at West Ham is under threat after a disappointing start to the season. West Ham are struggling to live up to their billing as Championship favourites and dropped to eighth after losing 3-1 to West Bromwich Albion on Saturday. West Ham are intent on an instant return to the Premier League after Nuno failed to save them from relegation last season, but the setback against West Brom put another dent in their promotion push. West Ham occupy the final playoff spot after consecutive defeats at home and are four points below second placed Swansea. Nuno is expected to be given time to turn the situation around but key figures have become increasingly impatient. The manager faced unrest from supporters during the West Brom game. Continue reading...

item.title: WSL talking points: Kang could have a problem and how long can Slegers hang on?
item.description: Arsenal dropped points again despite dominating while Lauren James had to go off in Chelsea’s 6-0 win at Charlton London City Lionesses may have lost 2-1 to champions Manchester City, but their performances and league position have shown their European aspirations are far from unrealistic. Aided by Arsenal’s poor start, London City are third in the WSL table and were frustrated to end the day with a six-point gap to the top two after dominating in Bromley. “It’s doubly frustrating, because I think the result was not the one we deserve,” said their coach, Eder Maestre. “Manchester City are more mature. They are more used to it. When you have this consistency and you are very used to playing these kinds of games, maybe you have more experience.” Maestre’s team have a three-point lead over fourth-placed Tottenham and if they continue their upwards trajectory and qualify for the Champions League, Uefa will be forced to tackle the possible scenario of two Michele Kang-owned clubs, London City and OL Lyonnes, qualifying sooner than they perhaps anticipated. item.title: Unai Simón caps myth-making week with another extraordinary night | Sid Lowe
item.description: Athletic’s win over Real Sociedad was culmination of six unique days for the Spain keeper after night at the Palladium For the third time in six days everyone got to their feet to hand a standing ovation to Unai Simón, dressed in all black, before the world. Named the best men’s goalkeeper on the planet, holding the Lev Yashin trophy, they had applauded him at the London Palladium on Monday night and before the game began at San Mamés, Bilbao, on Sunday. Now somewhere in the middle of it all, the ferocity of the 197th Basque derby, there was another moment, even more meaningful and more lasting, a cheer again giving way to something deeper: an appreciation for a man as well as his work closing a week that will be forever his. Which means it will be forever theirs too. Real Sociedad and Athletic Club had been doing battle for 72 minutes and it was 2-1 when Simon took off to make a save that denied Carlos Soler an equaliser and defied belief . As the ball flew off his palm, San Mamés exploded. And then it happened: never mind that Athletic still had a derby to win and a corner to defend, forget the fact that the lead was a single goal, the visitors relentless now and 25 minutes still to resist; at the stadium everyone calls the Cathedral , a place of ritual and liturgy like no other, the entire congregation, 50,092 people, started clapping. Started and did not stop. For a minute, maybe more, it was like the match that matters most didn’t matter at all, momentarily fading until it was just him and them together. Continue reading...

item.title: Premier League: 10 talking points from the weekend’s action
item.description: Marco Rose’s tactics are lifting Bournemouth, Roméo Lavia makes progress with Chelsea and Roberto De Zerbi gives youth a chance at Spurs Good defending is the mark of champions. At Anfield, where Arsenal had not won in the past 13 visits, Mikel Arteta followed the orthodoxy of locking down once his team took the lead. This time around, it proved successful. Arsenal did not allow the occasion or the stadium to get to them as they have on previous occasions. In April 2023, Granit Xhaka entangling with Trent Alexander-Arnold energised home fans previously despondent that Arsenal were 2-0 up. It finished 2-2. On Sunday, Liverpool zipped around zestfully, as Andoni Iraola requests, though the final-ball quality was lacking. That owed a great deal to the organisation of the Arsenal defence. Ahead of the last international break, Brighton set a blueprint for getting the better of Arsenal in winning 3-0 . Liverpool’s squad profile might have made a similar strategy possible though Iraola’s outfit is struggling to create chances in the same volume as Brighton or his Bournemouth team. item.title: Should Premier League strugglers stick or twist as pressure on managers mounts? | Andrew Beasley
item.description: Unusually, all clubs in the top flight have the same manager with whom they began the season – but the first sacking may not be far away No Premier League manager has yet lost his job this season. In only three of the past 10 campaigns was November reached without a club making a managerial change. The 2026-27 season commencing with 11 managers who were appointed at some point in 2026 has probably contributed to the early season stability. They have to be given a chance to fashion their side as they see fit. But with roughly a quarter of the season played and only one more round of fixtures before an international break, the first sacking may not be far away. Continue reading...

item.title: A phone-free Yellow Wall: are Dortmund urging fans to be present or policing them?
item.description: It makes sense that sports teams want to keep influencers out of their games. The battle some clubs are waging with their fans, however, is a different dilemma By all appearances, things on the Yellow Wall seemed as they always had been. The stadium announcer hollered out the first names of Borussia Dortmund’s starting lineup and the supporters responded with their last names, tens of thousands of voices bellowing as one. Dozens of black and yellow flags waved over Europe’s largest standing terrace, a mass of faces fixed on the field beneath them. And then Signal Iduna Park, sold out with 81,365 fans, roared when Max Beier’s lone goal led Dortmund to victory over Eintracht Frankfurt last Saturday, putting the home side even on points with Bayern Munich atop the Bundesliga standings. Continue reading...

item.title: Rodman rule has been revised but the fight to keep stars in the NWSL goes on | Moving the Goalposts
item.description: Gone are the eight criteria to be a High Impact Player so clubs can spend their money on whomever they want – and the solution makes sense When Washington plays Chicago this Sunday in DC, “Rowdy Audi” will probably be full. It will also be full when the post-season starts, should they lock up their top-four position with a positive result on Decision Day. Equipped with an accessible stadium in a big city, a proud fanbase and a formidable roster rife with players qualifying for the High Impact Player (HIP) rule’s initial criteria (including Trinity Rodman, who gave the rule its moniker), the Spirit hold sway in the attendance charts. But starting next season, everyone on the Spirit will qualify for the “Rodman Rule” . So will every player in NWSL. Announced Friday, NWSL settled a grievance with the league’s Players Association, who argued that the initial criteria violated federal labor law. Continue reading...

item.description: Plus: the longest home droughts, pre-Christmas goal centuries and the first official club websites Mail us with all of your questions and answers “Justin Seven-Seven came on in the 75th minute and then scored in the 77th minute for West Brom Under-21s against Sutton United in the National League Cup. You have probably already guessed my question, but has anyone else ever scored in the same minute as their name?” wonders Peter Skilton. Readers of a certain age may recall Didier Six , the mercurial French winger who had a brief spell at Aston Villa in 1984-85. A number of you mentioned some or all of the following sixth-minute goals, which includes two in consecutive seasons against Bordeaux: Valenciennes 2-1 Nancy (agg: 2-3) Coupe de France quarter-final, 1975-76 Valenciennes 3-2 Bordeaux Ligue 1, 1976-77 Lens 2-0 Bordeaux Ligue 1, 1977-78 VfB Stuttgart 5-1 Karlsruher Bundesliga, 1981-82 Bundesliga 71 goals in 18 games Champions League 18 goals in 6 games DFB-Pokal 10 goals in 3 games Franz Beckenbauer Supercup 2 goals in 1 game Continue reading...

item.title: An unmanageable club? Carrick the latest to suffer in Manchester United’s faded grandeur
item.description: Only Matt Busby and Alex Ferguson have truly succeeded in the Old Trafford hot seat with each casting uneasy shadows Should any football club fit the Great Man theory of history it is Manchester United. In the past 100 years, only Matt Busby and Alex Ferguson have knocked the club into shape. A pair of 20th-century Scotsmen, born 15 miles apart in Bellshill and Govan respectively, found the key. Otherwise, United has been a managerial dustbin, Michael Carrick the latest likely lobbed on the pile. Busby and Ferguson built the club around themselves, possessing the charisma to convince others that theirs was the path to follow. Carrick, an insider, a club man, is falling victim to the same isolation as his predecessors in failure . Bruno Fernandes and Lisandro Martínez going off-piste in TV interviews to depth charge Carrick were actually following club tradition. With glamour comes decadence, the faded grandeur that has so often chased a United manager out the door. Continue reading...

item.title: Kylian Mbappé apologises after being dropped by Chinese brands for Mao Zedong comment
item.description: Video appears to show Mao Zedong called a ‘dictator’ Dongpeng and Mengniu end deals with the player Kylian Mbappé has apologised after the Real Madrid forward was dropped by major Chinese brands for apparently joking about Mao Zedong in a video that has gone viral. There were also signs of broader repercussions, with the state-run Chinese digital newspaper The Paper reporting that public television was suspending broadcasts of matches from La Liga. The offending video shows Mbappé saying that the funniest internet meme he had seen involving him was of his face photoshopped on to that of “some guy – I think he’s a Chinese dictator”. This was an apparent reference to a meme of Mbappé superimposed on an image of Mao. Continue reading...

item.title: Mourinho’s plan comes together as Real Madrid relaunch with clásico statement | Sid Lowe
item.description: It was just like old times as José Mourinho ended a night at Camp Nou with a knee slide and three points José Mourinho had already done the por qu é? , the printout and the press conference no-show in under 100 days. Now he’s done a knee slide too, and in the perfect place: back where it all began and where it can all begin again. When Kylian Mbappé scored the first in the clásico on Sunday night, Real Madrid’s manager hardly moved, sitting in the shadow of the bench – but when the striker got the second to win it with time running out, that was different. Mourinho leapt into the light, throwing himself to the grass, the knees of a 63-year-old’s trousers muddy as a schoolboy’s, stuck his tongue out and pumped his fists. He does so love it when a plan comes together. To the right of him, the bench was emptying, subs joining the players in sprinting towards the south-west corner. As they leapt about, dodging the bottles thrown towards them from the end, way, way up in the furthest corner and stuck inside a glass box like a bunch of David Blaines, the small group of Madrid fans who had come were going mad. In the main stand, a thousand phones were raised. And 600 kilometres west, back in Boadilla, Thibaut Courtois was watching his teammates from the sofa at home, presumably wrapped in a blanket and cradling a cup of Lemsip. On the morning of the biggest game there is, he awoke with flu, forced to miss out. Continue reading...

item.title: The horse that ushered in Manchester United’s tragic arc | Jonathan Wilson
item.description: There’s plenty of blame to go around at Old Trafford. Like all downfalls it started with a seemingly small, unconnected moment Sign up for our free newsletter here And so here we are again, at that point as the nights draw in and Manchester United prepare to sack a manager . Autumn: season of mists, mellow fruitfulness and a crisis at Old Trafford. Sunday’s 3-0 home defeat to Bournemouth , coming on the back of last week’s 4-1 reverse against Como, made clear what many had feared from the moment Michael Carrick was given the job on a permanent basis: that he isn’t up to it. But then, who could be? When you’ve burned through a long list of managers in 13 years, it’s perhaps worth considering whether the manager is really the problem. Could some blame perhaps go to the director of football, Jason Wilcox, or the chief executive, Omar Berrada, the people making the appointments? Or perhaps to Sir Jim Ratcliffe, the cost-cutting tax exile and minority shareholder with responsibility for sporting operations? Or to the Glazer family, who plunged the club into debt with a leveraged buyout in 2005 and have since made calamitous decision after calamitous decision, reducing the most successful club in English league history to a mid-table laughing stock with a roof that leaks symbolically ? This is an extract from Soccer Desk, a newsletter from the Guardian US. Subscribe for free here . Continue reading...

item.title: Mbappé double secures Real Madrid late victory at Barcelona after Raphinha leveller
item.description: Thirteen years later, José Mourinho led Real Madrid into the Camp Nou as one team and them out again as another having secured the kind of late victory he loves and which opens up a whole new world. With just three minutes and the final reserves of energy remaining, a wonderful moment of skill from Jude Bellingham found Eduardo Camavinga and set them on one last run. Camavinga sprinted free, skilfully slipped Pau Cubarsí and pulled back for Kylian Mbappé to provide the finish, a little bit of history written. “The world that loves football will have stopped to watch this and they won’t have gone disappointed; this was two teams that played to win,” Mourinho said. It had been an intense, breathless ride, a proper battle, and it was his team who won it. Arriving right on time, Mbappé scored his second to make it 2-1, the Camp Nou falling quiet and their team given no time to react. They had drawn level after Mbappé’s opener, Raphinha scoring, but could not do it again. Continue reading...

item.title: Ian Holloway’s circus: why the manager’s antics are no laughing matter for fans
item.description: Swindon manager has a history of viral outbursts but fans want a united club and manager they can support In Ian Holloway’s often madcap managerial orbit, this was simply the latest in a steady succession of eccentric outbursts. Eyes bulging as he spoke, he boomed the letter “D” and promptly stabbed himself in the chest with an imaginary dagger. Next came the letter “M” alongside a blow from another invisible knife. Finally, a “W” followed by a jab to the heart. “Dead. Man. Walking,” he declared, pausing for effect between words and briefly falling into an Oscar-worthy zombie stupor. “That’s how it feels.” To an offbeat press conference genre containing seagulls following trawlers and self-proclaimed special ones, it was a crazy new entry worthy of its subsequent viral nature. Holloway at his finest. Continue reading...

item.title: James McClean: ‘Wearing the poppy was just never going to happen’
item.description: The former Republic of Ireland international on growing up in a community still reeling from the Troubles and the controversy that scarred his career “The perception of me is that, basically, I am a madman,” James McClean says calmly. “I’m outspoken. I’m a loudmouth. I’m very opinionated and I hate all things British. That’s from people who don’t know me. The reality is quite the opposite. I’m pretty boring. I go training, go home and switch off. A lot of my days are quite bland, quite basic.” McClean sounds as sane as he looks gaunt on a bleak Monday in Derry. He spent 14 years in English football and the fact that he is now at war with his own club, Derry City, can’t obscure the fact that he is the fifth-most-capped Republic of Ireland international, having played 103 times. “People define success in different ways,” he says, “but I’m the only footballer from the north of Ireland to win over 100 caps for Ireland. I played 150 Premier League games over five seasons, 800 professional games and won a lot of individual accolades. I count that as success and don’t look back with regrets.” Continue reading...

item.title: Next Generation 2021: why slow and steady sometimes wins the race
item.description: Our NextGen picks from five years ago show that breaking through early does not guarantee longevity or future success Read the full updates on our class of 2021 here and here In 2021, as every year, we picked 80 players from around the world who had a chance of making it in world football – 20 from the Premier League and 60 from the rest of the world – as part of our Next Generation series . We then follow these talented boys on their journeys for five years. Often it is almost impossible to predict how they will get on (OK, when Sid Lowe sent over Lamine Yamal in 2024 we had an inkling he might do well). The ball-playing central midfielder comes from a footballing family and academy staff believe his tactical awareness is born from growing up around the game. His father, Adam, played for Brighton and is now manager along the coast at Worthing FC, while Martin (his great uncle), Paul (his grandad), and Wally (his great grandad), all enjoyed careers as players. The youngest to play in the Bundesliga at 16 years and one day, youngest player to appear in the Champions League 17 days later, youngest goal scorer in Bundesliga 11 days after that and youngest player and youngest goal scorer for the Germany Under-21 team before he has turned 17. Continue reading...

item.content:encoded: Our NextGen picks from five years ago show that breaking through early does not guarantee longevity or future success Read the full updates on our class of 2021 here and here In 2021, as every year, we picked 80 players from around the world who had a chance of making it in world football – 20 from the Premier League and 60 from the rest of the world – as part of our Next Generation series . We then follow these talented boys on their journeys for five years. Often it is almost impossible to predict how they will get on (OK, when Sid Lowe sent over Lamine Yamal in 2024 we had an inkling he might do well). The ball-playing central midfielder comes from a footballing family and academy staff believe his tactical awareness is born from growing up around the game. His father, Adam, played for Brighton and is now manager along the coast at Worthing FC, while Martin (his great uncle), Paul (his grandad), and Wally (his great grandad), all enjoyed careers as players. The youngest to play in the Bundesliga at 16 years and one day, youngest player to appear in the Champions League 17 days later, youngest goal scorer in Bundesliga 11 days after that and youngest player and youngest goal scorer for the Germany Under-21 team before he has turned 17. Continue reading...

item.title: Transfer window verdict: how every Premier League club fared
item.description: The British transfer record was equalled and one club signed no fewer than 18 players in another hectic summer Bringing in Christos Tzolis, Bruno Guimarães and Ezri Konsa was a strong start to the window but could Arsenal’s failure to sign a marquee attacker cost them in the long run? They began targeting Morgan Rogers before pivoting to Vinícius Júnior when the England forward went to Chelsea, only to end up disappointed when Vinícius signed a new deal with Real Madrid. Julián Alvarez made clear he had no intention of joining from Atlético Madrid in the final days of the window and Arsenal kept their powder dry despite sanctioning the exits of Gabriel Jesus to Barcelona and Ethan Nwaneri to Borussia Dortmund. Should Gabriel Martinelli complete his move to Al-Hilal as expected in the coming days – the Saudi Pro League window remains open – a few injuries could leave Arteta short. Ed Aarons Continue reading...

item.title: Ousmane Dembélé quietly becomes the main man after long journey to the top
item.description: The Frenchman, who has been named the best male footballer in the world by the Guardian, has benefitted from PSG’s focus on the team rather than individuals What makes a good player great, and a great player the best? This question has been occupying me since 2014, when the Guardian first asked me to contribute to its inaugural Next Generation feature . My job was to look for a France-based talent born in 1997 who could go on to have a stellar career. After a great deal of research, I narrowed it down from my shortlist of five by asking questions not about the players’ football ability, but about other attributes: resilience, adaptability, decision-making, creativity, work ethic, response to feedback and willingness to learn. Qualities we cannot see, and are harder to measure. Continue reading...

item.title: Aitana Bonmatí makes Guardian top 100 history with third title in a row
item.description: The margin may have got smaller but the brilliant Spanish midfielder makes it a hat-trick of No 1 finishes They say the best things come in threes, and Aitana Bonmatí has written herself into the Guardian’s top 100 history as the first player to finish at the top of the tree for a third consecutive year. Last year the majestic midfielder emulated her Barcelona and Spain teammate Alexia Putellas by winning for a second year running , but the 27-year-old has now gone one better, establishing herself once again at the top of the women’s game. Continue reading...
